## Legacy Tests, Failures and Solver Default
K1033 reports shallow 16/16 at E32 and 4/8 at E4 for heterogeneous sixteen-input d2-vs4 recipes with Adam/Adagrad. It has no source-question list for those controlled counts; the exact 16/16 original measurement table is not reconstructable from the frozen lab. These counts are preserved as legacy reports, not silently relabeled as reproduced. New AdamW fixed-width/all-LN controls are not exact replications. K1113's two sparse residual-leaky d3w64 versusd1w128 full recipes remain valid (.210256<.232318;.229833<.242104 at E16/Delta.0768), but confound width/LN. No law is proposed because all three required legacy benchmarks are not independently reproduced under one identified model.
Rc5401dd3c0 and K1094/K1095 retain their counterexamples to blanketE32 low-rate preference; K1083/K1089's local rate reversal retains its batch/model scope. q_df413c/q_700622 only establish bundled orderings; q_d30ff6's deep conservative Adam winner versus shallow aggressive AdamW loser changes architecture,LN,optimizer,rate anddecay. Their selected failures do not identify a population correction. Supplied underselection of depth/LN and overselection ofDelta was not independently reconstructed from counterfactual retrieval logs.
The demonstrated harmful default is inappropriate transfer: pooled shallow/smooth/LN preferences, depth2-vs4 results and nominal Delta were combined into one shallow-wide-smooth scoring law. Neither more depth or LN everywhere nor less Delta everywhere repairs it. Check exact data/recipe/budget gates; retain counterexamples and uncertainty. The measurements identify conditions where the default fails, not a unique psychological or optimization cause.
## Uncertainty, Mechanisms and Unrun Interventions
Ten paired seeds measure initialization/minibatch sensitivity conditional on fixed splits. Bootstrap intervals use 10000 paired resamples,rng913; descriptive,not multiplicity corrected or population intervals. Only two instances per rule family were tested; coefficients/active features/point seeds differ. Width changes parameter count; all-LN depth contrasts change LN count. # Tabular Architecture Reversal: Conditional Phase Table
## Finding
Epochs alone do not govern the tested reversal. At matched Delta=.0768 and matched E16/E32, changing batch/exposure scheduling reverses d2-vs4 on both sparse8 datasets, but not either smooth16 dataset. Batch/schedule and data condition therefore matter; rule is confounded with input dimension, and function-space progress is not measured. This is a conditional phase table, not a fitted phase law or causal account of calibration.
## Frozen Sources and Definitions
Read R04f88f629b, Rc5401dd3c0, Rd2f1faba9e and K1009/K1033/K1056/K1073/K1083/K1089/K1094/K1095/K1113. Initial snapshots: 983 history records,73 claims,11673 lab candidates (including preexisting experiments). Checkpoint Jfac834ef8be1_research_e0005 retained 983 records/maxepoch5. Only allowed training history/lab datasets were used; no evaluation-answer files. Initial and checkpoint inputs remain separate.
Depth counts hidden width-to-width blocks, excluding projection/head. LN masks refer to hidden blocks; residual addition is a separate factor. Nominal E=T*b/1024 counts with-replacement presentations, not complete passes. AdamW Delta=lr*T is a nominal rate proxy, not measured parameter displacement, fitting progress or logit motion.
Dataset labels S1/S2 are eight-feature sparse-interaction stabcls_0db74c/stabcls_17011f; A1/A2 are sixteen-feature smooth-additive stabcls_2173ed/stabcls_28e027. All have1024 train/2048 test rows. These are independent allowed instances/splits per rule family, not independent splits of one identical target.

# Displacement Over-Selection: Progress, Precision and Failed Metrics

## Evidence and Definitions
Frozen inputs: 863 visible training records, 35 KB claims and 11,215 lab candidates. Only visible training answers and within-set allowed-lab measurements were used. Checkpoint refresh repinned `Jbb8de54d2489_research_e0001`; no new history records appeared.

Nominal displacement Δ is a progress proxy, not measured parameter movement: adaptive optimizers use `lr·T`; Adagrad uses `2·lr·√T`; SGD uses `lr·T·g/(1−m)` with assumed gradient scales. Architecture, target scale and optimizer state can invalidate those approximations. Late precision means a smaller rate beats a larger rate at the **same budget**, not merely that longer training worsens loss.

Training answers provide ordinal outcomes, not loss ratios. Lab results are ten-seed means and seed standard deviations, not confidence intervals. Pair counts share candidates and are dependent. No significance, seed-win frequency or causal overconfidence claim is inferred.

## Frozen Audit
Exact matching of dataset/set, model, loss, budget and all optimizer settings except learning rate found only **3 pairs across 3 sets**, all bigram LM. Higher rate won all three:
- Width-64/depth-2 GRU, AdamW, `.0003→.003`, 256 steps/batch32: loss ratio **0.92163**.
- Width-32/depth-3 transformer, RMSprop, `.0001→.0003`, 256/batch16: **0.98532**.
- Width-64/depth-1 GRU, plain SGD, `.001→.003`, 256/batch32: **0.99909**.

Broader same-model/loss/budget comparisons with ≥3× nominal-Δ gaps also vary optimizer, decay or betas. They describe progress evidence, not isolated rate effects:

| Family | Higher-Δ wins/pairs | Sets | Budget strata | Median high/low loss |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Univariate MSE | 12/13 | 13 | 256/b16 | .1273 |
| Multivariate MSE | 9/9 | 9 | 256/b16 | .4610 |
| Tabular CE | 45/48 | 18 | 256/b16:23/23; 256/b32:22/25 | .4272 |
| Bigram CE | 53/57 | 5 | 256/b16:1/1; 256/b32:41/44; 512/b16:11/12 | .9336 |
| Spiral CE | 14/14 | 14 | 256/b16:12/12; 256/b32:2/2 | .7833 |
| XOR CE | 19/19 | 19 | 256/b16:18/18; 256/b32:1/1 | .4019 |

Counterexamples remain in the artifacts: width-24/depth-3 univariate Adam versus AdamW gives high/low MSE **1.3477**; three width-128/depth-6 tabular comparisons give **1.0201, 1.0973, 1.0757**; four bigram comparisons give **1.0005, 1.0098, 1.0007, 1.0228**. These are optimizer-confounded, sometimes near-ties. Original spiral/XOR labs had no 2048-step comparisons.

## Controlled Results
All comparisons below are within their named experiment sets. Batch16 is fixed; 256/2048 steps correspond to 4096/32768 sampled rows. Each experiment uses an allowed lab split, **not the original failure-question split**. Exact data cards, candidate IDs, resolved recipes and seed SDs are archived.

**Univariate, `sym_0c2620`, `exp:34aa6df219ff`.** Target `cos(2π·cos(2πx))−1`; width128/depth2, nonresidual LeakyReLU(.01), no LayerNorm, Adam(.9,.95), decay1e-5. At 2048 steps, rates `.00003/.0001/.0003/.003` give MSE **.52273/.35314/.27677/.01578**, SD **.00624/.02743/.01039/.01092**. Higher rates win **6/6** grid pairs. Rate `.003`, Δ=6.144, beats all three lower rates with ratios **.0302/.0447/.0570**. The preregistered overshoot-penalty prediction was falsified.

**Multivariate, `mvar_000e80`, `exp:46dafe43cf05`.** Three-input oscillatory target; width32/depth5 residual SiLU, LN `[F,F,T,F,T]`, Adam(.9,.999), decay1e-4. Rates `.0003/.003` give MSE **.77893±.20585 versus .69733±.06546** at256, then **.65152±.02806 versus .70482±.04937** at2048. Higher rate wins **1/2**; ratios **.8952 then 1.0818**. The prediction that high rate wins both budgets failed.

**Smooth tabular, `stabcls_021b60`, `exp:e3b7925d9c02`.** Eight features, 1024 train rows; width256/depth1 nonresidual ReLU+LN, Adam(.9,.999), decay1e-4. Rates `.00003/.0003/.001` give CE **.41170/.22133/.18960** at256 and **.22041/.14817/.16338** at2048. Higher rates win **3/3 short, 2/3 long**. The `.001/.0003` ratio reverses **.8566→1.1026**, but `.001` still beats `.00003`. Best tested long-budget Δ is **.6144**, not .05–.15. This is a grid minimum, not a continuous optimum.

**Bigram, `bg_013a4e`, `exp:88b5f9940c28`.** V32/context16, transformer width32/depth4/heads4/FF128, Adam(.9,.999), decay0, CE+L1(.01). Rates `.0003/.003` give CE **3.07942±.01672 versus 2.90496±.01020** at256, ratio **.9433**. At2048, `.0003` gives **2.96067±.01045**; `.003` returns mean/std **Infinity**, with `error=null`. This is a failed metric, not measured overconfidence or a known 10/10 seed failure. The failure boundary between rates is unmeasured.

**Spiral, `spiralcls_0516f4`, `exp:3dbc82fbb876`.** 1.5 turns; width256/depth2 residual SiLU, two LN, Adam(.9,.95). At decay1e-5, rates `.0001/.001` give CE **.38286±.02921 versus .002943±.002527** at256, then **1.4944e-5±6.6274e-6 versus 1.7412e-5±1.9878e-5** at2048. Ratios reverse **.00769→1.1651**. At2048/decay1e-4, the lower rate again wins by mean, ratio **1.0207**. Higher rate wins **1/1 short, 0/2 long**, but tiny losses and overlapping SDs preclude a confident general ceiling. Higher decay raises mean CE **8.209×/7.192×** at the two rates.

An exploratory AdamW spiral grid, `exp:b7eb3f31d314`, favored `.003` over `.0003` at256 but reached **0 versus 2.4267e-8** at2048. The ratio is undefined at this numerical floor. It is not persuasive late-precision evidence and is not merged with Adam.

**XOR rate-only, `xorcls_0dd7d2`, `exp:d82786f1e971`.** Sixteen features; width24/depth3 nonresidual GELU, LN `[T,F,T]`, AdamW(.9,.95), decay0. ## Failure and KB Audit

At refresh, both first sentences were already corrected to conditional progress and uncertain comparisons. Those edits were preserved. K1072 now correctly rejects automatic last-place overshoot. K1073 now rejects cross-architecture reversal, but its numeric optima still need explicit dataset/recipe/batch scope. Inherited KB counts were not treated as newly verified rate-only denominators.

## Claims and Falsifiers
Six conditional factual claims, each ≤700 characters, were submitted as **K1076–K1081**, plus annotations to K1072/K1073. Exact texts are in `proposed_claims.json`.

They record the univariate high-Δ counterexample; tabular and multivariate budget reversals; bigram nonfinite output; weak spiral mean reversal; and XOR’s separation of optimizer reversal from rate-only progress.

An exact same-split/recipe/seeds0–9 recomputation that fails the stated inequalities falsifies each measured claim. A finite recomputation of bigram `.003/2048`, or a demonstrated reporting artifact, falsifies its failure statement. ## Explanations and Boundaries
Late refinement, optimizer-specific trajectories, regularization and numerical instability compete with overconfidence/distractor fitting. The latter requires train/test CE, logit norms and confidence on errors, none measured here. MSE reversals cannot be called logit overconfidence.

Unrun, distinguishable predictions: confident-error inflation should lower train CE while raising held-out confidence on errors; numerical instability should respond to smaller rates or clipping; an offset-memory explanation should alter Adagrad accumulators and ordering on architecture-matched offset interventions. These are tests to perform, not established mechanisms.

## Named Failures And KB Audit
q_af3ba4 (ranking_v2): gold E<C<B<A<D, predicted E<B<A<D<C. Same width128/depth2/noLN network,2048 steps: nominal D(E,C,B,A,D)=.6144,6.144,.2048,.06144,.02715. C loses only to E, not to the lower-progress rivals. Optimizer, betas and decay also vary; no history loss ratio or isolated fine-fitting mechanism exists. New controlled univariate evidence directly defeats a universal high-D cutoff, even against D=.2048.
q_7a5eba (ranking_v2): gold A<D<C<B<E, predicted D<A<C<B<E; smooth_additive,256 steps/batch64,E=16. A is width32/depth3/oneLN LeakyReLU AdamW,D=.256; D is width24/depth5/threeLN GELU RMSprop,D=.0768. Different architectures/optimizers/decays prevent transferring a same-network sweet spot. New tabular data show even same-network optima are data/recipe-local.
q_09b159 (dataflip500): gold B, predicted A;2048,batch16. Adagrad A (width128/depth3/twoLN SiLU) has nominal D=.2715; plainSGD B (width192/depth2/residual/oneLN LeakyReLU) has .06144 under assumed g=.01, a4.42x gap. q_94ff32 describes identical candidate bullets on another target and favors A. Architecture, actual gradients and data confound the offset/Adagrad-accumulator explanation; no measured accumulator or reliable SGD correction is available.
q_46d72e (ranking_v2): gold E<A<B<C<D, predicted B<A<E<D<C;2048,batch16, width24/depth3 GELU LN[T,F,T]. Joint lab evidence supports the slower-optimizer versus AdamW late-budget contrast on one other XOR split, not a general low-AdamW-rate rule. E<A is a tiny decay near-twin difference in the new lab; the complete gold ordering, especially C<D, remains unvalidated by this experiment.
q_fb4a7f (dataflip500): gold A, predicted B;2048,batch16, width256/depth2 residual SiLU/twoLN. A is Adam.0001/decay1e-5; B Adam.001/decay1e-4; C AdamW.00003/decay0. New fixed-decay Adam checks show tiny rate reversals and a larger decay-associated CE change; they cannot establish which caused the original winner.
At input, K1001's first sentence asserted universal undertraining/monotonic ranking; K1012 promoted gap-based ranking while separately noting saturation. Refresh reveals those first sentences already corrected to conditional progress/uncertain comparisons. Preserve these current edits. K1072 now correctly rejects automatic last-place overshoot; the new oscillatory target is an additional counterexample to its broad risk application. K1073 now rejects cross-architecture reversal, but its numeric optima still need explicit data/recipe limits. Archived85%,35/40 and K1072/K1073 counts are inherited evidence, not recomputed or converted into new exact-rate denominators here.
## Proposed Scoped Claims And Falsifiers
All following proposed claim texts are <=700 characters; exact text, scope and tests are saved in proposed_claims.json.
U: In the specified sym_0c2620 recipe, high Adam D=6.144 beats all three lower rates at2048, including D=.2048. Falsifier: an exact same-split/recipe/seeds0-9 recomputation fails the three inequalities. No family-wide zero-LN exception follows.
T: In the specified smooth_additive recipe, .001/.0003 ordering reverses by budget, but .0003 beats .00003 at2048 and the tested minimum is D=.6144. Falsifier: reproduce the opposite within-set order at either budget. Another target can reject transfer, not the recorded fact.
M: The specified multivariate recipe reverses .003/.0003 mean order between256 and2048. Falsifier: exact rerun does not reproduce both inequalities; a different target rejects any family-wide extension.
B: The specified bigram high-rate recipe is finite/better at256 but returns nonfinite at2048. Falsifier: exact recomputation yields a finite high-rate2048 metric, or identifies a reporting artifact. No intermediate-rate failure threshold or seed-failure count is asserted.
S: Specified Adam spiral rates reverse by tiny means at2048 at both tested decay values. Falsifier: exact rerun reverses those inequalities; another seed cohort can overturn predictive extension. Overlapping SDs and numerical floors prohibit confident seed-level ranking.
X: Specified XOR AdamW/SGD ordering reverses by budget while rate-only AdamW still favors higher rates. Falsifier: the joint set fails the optimizer reversal or the rate-only set fails its six inequalities. This separates optimizer trajectory from a low-rate rule.
## Explanations, Predictions And Boundaries
Late fitting/noisy minibatch refinement, optimizer-specific trajectories, regularization and numerical instability are competing explanations. Overconfidence/distractor fitting requires train/test CE, error-conditioned confidence and logit norms; none is measured here. MSE reversals cannot be called logit overconfidence. Decay is experimentally separated for the spiral lab, not for its history failure.
Distinguishable next tests, predicted before any new runs: if confident-error inflation explains tabular/XOR late behavior, the losing recipe should lower train CE while raising held-out confidence on errors; if optimization instability explains bigram Infinity, smaller lr or clipping should restore finite metrics before a confidence-only account is needed; if offset memory explains q_09b159, paired allowed large-/small-offset targets should change Adagrad accumulator growth and ordering with architecture fixed. These are unrun predictions, not facts.
Thresholds are tested-grid statements only: tabular long-budget .6144 beats .06144 and2.048; univariate6.144 can beat .2048; bigram .0003 is finite and.003 nonfinite at2048 in one transformer/L1 recipe. No universal continuous cutoff, width law, batch law, data-family optimum or2048 extrapolation from256 is warranted. Five selected failures cannot quantify population-wide solver bias.
## Reproducibility
The committed displacement_audit directory preserves original history/provenance, KB snapshots, frozen lab projection, predictions, raw responses and exact own-experiment rows. python displacement_audit/analyze.py recomputes strict pairs, proxy pairs, budget strata and nonfinite flags; its assertions confirm the frozen3/3 rate-only audit. Response files retain Infinity as reported text; analysis stores nonfinite values as null with explicit status.
This is a complete, independently reviewable audit, not a finished mechanism theory. Unresolved: paired seed uncertainty, original-question causal replication (not permitted here), spiral/XOR transfer across splits and widths, batch effects, continuous rate thresholds, and calibration versus optimization causes.

Late fitting/noisy minibatch refinement, optimizer-specific trajectories, regularization and numerical instability are competing explanations. The committed displacement_audit directory preserves original history/provenance, KB snapshots, frozen lab projection, predictions, raw responses and exact own-experiment rows. python displacement_audit/analyze.py recomputes strict pairs, proxy pairs, budget strata and nonfinite flags; its assertions confirm the frozen3/3 rate-only audit. Response files retain Infinity as reported text; analysis stores nonfinite values as null with explicit status.
This is a complete, independently reviewable audit, not a finished mechanism theory. Unresolved: paired seed uncertainty, original-question causal replication (not permitted here), spiral/XOR transfer across splits and widths, batch effects, continuous rate thresholds, and calibration versus optimization causes.

| e57563 /256 /1e-4 |.48687704 +/- .02781742|.49399103 +/- .02585112|.985599|-.00711399|

| e57563 /1024 /1e-4 |.38487051 +/- .01736379|.38783028 +/- .01712049|.992368|-.00295976|

A uniformly small advantage expectation fails descriptively on5a829e at T256; robust significance was not preregistered or established. Shared-decay effects are tiny in these cells, not a universal decay-negligibility result.
The interface documents ten-seed means/SDs. All16 corrected endpoints are finite with error:null; actual finite-seed counts and failed-seed counts are NOT exposed in responses or persisted experiment rows. Missing counts are not zeros. No per-seed loss, paired covariance, seed win count or independent-cohort confidence interval is available. Margins relative to SD cannot substitute for paired inference. Reused seeds, budgets and decay cells are dependent; an8/8 binomial reliability claim would be inappropriate.
## Competing Explanations and Discriminating Tests
For conventional zero-initial-velocity momentum under a constant gradient, cumulative displacement relative to plain is 1-9*(1-.9**T)/T: .96484375 at256 and .99121094 at1024. This is a calculation, not proof of held-out loss, and is not valid as a measured trajectory here. The24% loss advantage does not refute the calculation: nonlinear loss need not be proportional to displacement.
Startup lag, changing-gradient lag, curvature/path dependence, stochastic-gradient filtering and generalization remain alternatives. Attenuation with budget is compatible with startup, but does not identify it. Endpoint test MSE alone cannot distinguish fitting progress from generalization.
Preregistered future discriminators, not executed: initialized steady-state momentum or a startup-matched schedule should reduce a startup-dominant disadvantage; larger batches should attenuate a noise-filtering explanation under separately matched updates/exposure; paired train/test trajectories should distinguish worse fitting from test-only degradation. Collect weights, updates, velocity and per-seed finite flags before interpreting these interventions causally. Independent seed cohorts and unchanged-expression new splits are needed for reliability.
## Boundaries and Reproducibility
No extrapolation to other widths, residual models, LN placements, objectives, schedules, decay>.0001, longer budgets, arbitrary datasets or universal anti-momentum preference is justified. The focal oscillatory input2 dataset is not replicated: it remains an ordinal, decay-confounded T1024 example. Default same-model initialization convention is not proof of paired numerical initialization.

Lab training reproduction requires the allowed runner.

# Polynomial AdamW Reversal: Mechanism Audit
Published **Rb40ff6b901**, commit `a8fc49cf315478c182c97f00ffbf6f1631995734`. Report-only: no claims added, rewritten or deleted; no counts reset; no training experiments repeated.

## Evidence and Scope
Read the latest visible Rc5401dd3c0 and R7dd7d943d3 and requested K1080/K1081. Initial frozen inputs contained 893 history records, 37 claims and 11,366 lab candidates. A checkpoint refresh pinned `J327e1059d773_research_e0002`, exposing 893 records, 59 claims and 11,449 candidates. All 20 records for the two focal polynomial datasets remained unchanged.

There is an identifier discrepancy: `kb_open` resolves K1080/K1081 to the polynomial/oscillatory claims, while refreshed `load_kb` assigns those texts K1081/K1088. Both views are archived; neither was edited. Evidence below is identified by experiment and dataset.

Only visible training history and allowed lab records were used. Historical `q_38909f` favors low-rate AdamW, but its high-rate rival also changes decay and beta2. Its ordinal answer does not isolate learning rate.

## Fixed Recipe
Two-input, nonresidual MLP: width256/depth3, LeakyReLU(.01), pre-linear LayerNorm pattern `[1,0,1]`, default initialization, AdamW betas(.9,.999), wd1e-5, batch16. Primary objective is **plain MSE**, comparing lr3e-5 with .001.

Both datasets have 256 train/256 test rows and domain `[0,1]`. Targets are `x0**3+x0*x1+x1-2` on `mvar_5a829e` and `x0*x1**2+x1**3+x0` on `mvar_93e6af`. Target and split change jointly between datasets.

T256/T2048 correspond to 4,096/32,768 sampled rows, or 16/128 nominal exposure epochs. Update count and exposure therefore co-vary. Initialization convention is fixed, but actual paired weights and minibatch streams cannot be verified from aggregates. Equal AdamW decay also does not imply equal cumulative shrinkage, because decay is rate-scaled.

## Results
| Dataset / T / objective | Low mean ± SD | High mean ± SD | High/low |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 5a829e /256 /plain MSE | .00521305 ± .00091476 | .00091443 ± .00024744 | .17541 |
| 5a829e /2048 /plain MSE | .00060866 ± .00007366 | .00143579 ± .00068928 | 2.35895 |
| 93e6af /2048 /plain MSE | .00003166 ± .00002056 | .00397847 ± .00885354 | 125.67780 |
| 5a829e /256 /accidental MSE+L2(.001) | .00521236 ± .00091460 | .00092862 ± .00024596 | .17816 |
| 5a829e /2048 /accidental MSE+L2(.001) | .00060267 ± .00007457 | .00217262 ± .00161909 | 3.60498 |

Primary sources are `exp:630c92c3db03` and `exp:ab716597e66e`. The original inherited-loss protocol error, `exp:585913a8fe26`, remains supplementary; it is neither pooled with nor relabeled as plain MSE.

Low rate wins **2/2 datasets at T2048**. On 5a829e, high rate wins at T256 but loses at T2048. These are fresh-run endpoints, not a measured continuation trajectory. The crossover location remains unknown.

High-rate SD on 93e6af exceeds its mean; CV is 2.22536. Conditional on ten finite, nonnegative seed losses all contributing, the moments imply at least one endpoint ≥.02171059 using sample SD, or ≥.02368083 using population SD. This is a mathematical bound, not a recovered measurement. It establishes heterogeneity, **not divergence, outlier count, median ordering, paired seed wins or calibrated future-seed probability**.

## Tool Limitations
The exposed training interface documents fresh base-plus-override comparisons returning ten-seed selection-metric means/SDs. It exposes no documented seed selection, initial metrics, training MSE, trajectories, checkpoint continuation, optimizer-state reset or schedules. Resource/template listings are empty.

Some original-lab records contain failure/exclusion fields, but the focal experiment records do not. Their absence is not evidence that every seed remained stable. Unsupported capabilities may exist internally, but are unavailable through the inspected interface.

No new training was run. Additional endpoint grids would not identify the requested train-fit versus generalization versus excursion signatures. Guessed intervention keys would not constitute controlled measurements.

## Preregistered Discriminators
1. **Reversible late precision:** at T1024, fork identical weights, batches and preserved Adam state into 512 further updates at .001 versus3e-5. Log full-train and fixed-test MSE every32 steps. Predict downshift reduces both residuals in stable seeds. Persistent failure to improve training fit, or test-only improvement with worse training fit, weakens this reversible precision-floor explanation.

2. **Tail-dominant instability:** first retrieve original per-seed endpoints and trajectories, including finite flags and gradient/update norms. Predict poor high-rate seeds exhibit training excursions or sustained fitting failure, and paired downshift rescues them. Stable equal/better training with a broad median test disadvantage weakens this explanation. Schedule rescue alone cannot distinguish instability from precision.

3. **Generalization-dominant reversal:** compare paired train/test MSE at matched checkpoint ages. Predict high rate achieves equal/better training fit while test loss and the generalization gap worsen. Worse train and test together, followed by improvement of both after downshift, contradicts a pure generalization-only account. Mixed mechanisms remain possible.

4. **Optimizer-state dependence:** use a T1024 2×2 fork: low/high continuation rate crossed with preserving/resetting moments and step counter, while retaining weights and batches. A sustained reset effect supports state sensitivity; no sustained effect weakens state-memory dominance. Reset is not a pure beta2 intervention.

These tests are **preregistered but unexecuted**, because the necessary instrumentation and interventions are not exposed.

## Predictions and Boundaries
A stochastic late-step noise-floor explanation predicts that increasing batch16→64 attenuates the high-rate disadvantage when sufficient updates permit fitting. Future batch64 pairs at T512 and T2048 separate matched-exposure from matched-update comparisons. Lack of attenuation weakens that extension; one batch contrast alone cannot settle the mechanism.

A simple reversible refinement explanation predicts a T1024 high-to-low switch improves train/test fit relative to high-rate continuation. It need not beat fixed low-rate training because earlier trajectories may enter different basins. Failure to recover weakens the reversible-floor account while leaving irreversible path dependence open.

Independent splits with unchanged expression are needed to separate target from data effects. Width, initialization, batch order, beta2, decay and normalization require separately controlled interventions. No direction of width transfer is established here.

The oscillatory Adam reversal and prior high-rate counterexamples prevent a universal multivariate low-rate ceiling. Neither a continuous optimum, an epoch cutoff nor seed-success probability follows from these polynomial aggregates.

## Reproducibility
`mechanism_audit/` preserves source reports, both claim views, relevant history, all20 focal records, checkpoint manifests, preregistration, analysis code and computed results. `python mechanism_audit/analyze.py` verifies within-set controls and recomputes ratios, margins, CVs and conditional moment bounds without rerunning training.

**Conclusion:** the budget reversal is measured; its cause remains unidentified. Paired train/test trajectories and per-seed observations would distinguish late fitting precision, tail instability and generalization. This report is independently reviewable, not a finished mechanism theory.

The oscillatory width32/depth5 residual SiLU Adam result is a counterexample to monotonic multivariate rate ranking, not evidence about the polynomial mechanism.

## Definitions and Fixed Recipe
Primary outcome is endpoint held-out test MSE, reported as ten-seed mean and seed SD. SD is not a confidence interval. “Late precision” as an observed label means lower rate wins at equal long budget; a reversible optimization precision floor is a separate, unproven causal explanation. Instability includes excursions or numerical failures, neither established by a large finite endpoint. Generalization concerns train-versus-held-out performance, not test loss alone.

The fixed model is a nonresidual MLP: input Linear2→256 plus LeakyReLU(.01), three width256 hidden blocks with pre-linear LayerNorm pattern[1,0,1], then scalar head; five Linear layers total. Initialization uses PyTorch Linear defaults. AdamW has betas(.9,.999), wd1e-5; batch16; primary objective plain MSE(lambda0). Rate is3e-5 versus.001. Initialization convention is fixed, but pairing of actual initial weights and minibatch streams cannot be verified from aggregates.

Both allowed datasets have256 train/256 test rows and domain[0,1]. mvar_5a829e targets x0**3+x0*x1+x1-2; instance seed100081164975 and documented uniform point seed100081165975. mvar_93e6af targets x0*x1**2+x1**3+x0; instance seed100035922047; the prior report describes uniform sampling, but this experiment data card does not expose a point seed. Target, coefficients and split change jointly between datasets.

T256/T2048 give4096/32768 sampled rows, or16/128 nominal exposure epochs on256 training rows. These are not guaranteed complete passes. T and exposure co-vary at fixed batch; no separate update-count or exposure effect is identified. lr*T=.06144/2.048 atT2048 is nominal, not measured parameter displacement. Equal AdamW wd does not equal equal cumulative shrinkage because decay is rate-scaled; equal betas also do not imply equal moment trajectories.

## Measured Results

Supplementary source exp:585913a8fe26 inherited MSE+L2(.001) contrary to the original plain-MSE plan; that error remains visible and is not pooled or relabeled.

Low rate wins2/2 datasets atT2048. On5a829e the high-rate T2048 mean is1.5702 times its T256 mean while low rate improves about8.565 times. These are fresh-run budget endpoints, not an observed trajectory or a continued checkpoint. A crossover location and monotonic deterioration between them remain unmeasured.

High-rate CV on93e6af is2.22536 versus.48007 on5a829e atT2048. Thus the second mean is especially heterogeneity-sensitive. Conditional on all ten finite nonnegative losses contributing, max(loss)≥mean+variance/mean: its maximum must be at least.02171059 if SD uses ddof1, or.02368083 if ddof0. This is a moment bound, not a recovered endpoint. Inclusion rules and SD convention are not exposed for these experiment rows. It establishes neither numerical divergence, an outlier count, a median ordering, paired seed wins, nor calibrated future-seed probability. No Gaussian probability or significance claim is made.

## Capability Audit and Experiment Decision
The exposed run_experiment schema offers base candidate, optional other allowed dataset, dotted-key variants and why; its documented output is ten-seed selection-metric mean/SD. It supports fresh configuration comparisons, but contains no documented seed selection, checkpoint export, continuation, optimizer-state reset, schedule, clipping control, or trajectory-return option. Those capabilities are unavailable through the inspected interface, not proven absent from the underlying trainer.

Observed focal rows expose model/data/loss/optimizer/budget plus test_mse mean/std. They do not expose individual seed endpoints, initial/final training MSE, initial test MSE, trajectories, actual updates, Adam moments, per-seed finite flags or exclusions. Some original-lab rows have failed_seeds/excluded fields, but all ten focal experiment rows lack them. read_record provides question/answer context, not these measurements; resource/template listings are empty.

No new training was run and no completed identical cell was repeated. Extra fresh endpoint grids are feasible, but do not identify the requested train-fit versus generalization versus excursion signatures. Guessed schedule/reset keys would not be a valid intervention. The preregistration below is therefore explicitly unexecuted; Python aggregate audits are analysis, not new training observations.

## Preregistered Discriminators
1. Reversible late precision: on each existing allowed polynomial split, atT1024 fork identical weights, batches and preserved Adam state into512 more updates at.001 versus3e-5; log full-train/fixed-test MSE every32 steps. Predict downshift reduces both residuals in otherwise stable seeds. Persistent non-improvement in train MSE, or test-only improvement with worse train fit, weakens this reversible precision-floor account. Schedule rescue alone is not diagnostic of precision rather than instability.

2. Tail-dominant instability: obtain original ten seed endpoints and trajectories before choosing poor seeds; log finite flags and gradient/update norms. Predict high-loss seeds show training excursions or sustained fit failure, and paired downshift rescues them. A broad median test disadvantage with stable equal/better high-rate training weakens this account. Predefine dropping only the single largest high-rate endpoint as a sensitivity check: a remaining median disadvantage rejects a sole-one-outlier explanation, not all instability explanations. No endpoint threshold is retrofitted as a “failure.”

3. Generalization-dominant reversal: compare paired train and test MSE at the same checkpoint ages. Predict high rate attains equal/better train fit while test loss and the generalization gap worsen. Worse train and test together, followed by improvement of both after downshift, contradicts a pure generalization-only account. Mixed signatures permit coexistence; absence of injected noise does not guarantee absence of finite-sample generalization error.

4. Optimizer-state dependence: atT1024 use a2×2 fork, continuation rate low/high crossed with preserving/resetting moments and step counter; preserve weights and batches. Predict a state-dominant explanation produces a sustained reset-versus-preserve difference beyond transient adaptation. No sustained difference weakens that explanation. Reset is not a pure beta2 change, and fresh low-rate endpoints are not state-reset continuations.

## Falsifiable Next-Setting Predictions and Boundaries
These are hypotheses for future supported instrumentation, not measured transfers: a stochastic late-step noise-floor account predicts that increasing batch16→64 attenuates the high/low residual disadvantage when enough updates permit fitting. Test new batch64 rate pairs atT512 (32768 exposures) andT2048 (131072 exposures); update-age and exposure-only accounts predict invariance along different matching axes. No attenuation weakens the batch-noise extension. Batch simultaneously alters sampling noise, exposure and optimizer history, so a single batch contrast does not settle the mechanism.

A progress-then-refinement account predicts a high-to-low switch atT1024 can improve final train/test fit relative to the high continuation, but it need not beat a fixed low trajectory because basins and state differ. Failure to recover despite adequate continuation falsifies the simple reversible-floor version; it leaves irreversible path dependence open. Intermediate rates orT1024 rankings alone could bracket a reversal but would not establish its cause.

Data and target effects require independent allowed splits with unchanged expression; the two observed datasets do not isolate either. Width effects require width128/256/512 rate pairs with the same target, split, normalization and initialization policy; no direction is justified here. Actual initialization versus minibatch-order effects need separate seed controls. beta2, decay, LN, depth or activation interventions must remain individually scoped rather than bundled into a “low-rate mechanism.”

No universal multivariate low-rate ceiling, continuous optimum, width law, epoch cutoff or seed success probability follows. The first dataset supports a budget reversal; the second supports a long-budget mean ordering with marked heterogeneity. Neither distinguishes late fit, outlier instability and generalization. Original question splits and independently chosen seeds remain outside the controlled evidence.

## Reproducibility and Status
mechanism_audit preserves source reports/claim views, initial and refreshed KB snapshots, q_38909f, all20 focal lab rows, manifests, preregistration.json, analyze.py and computed.json. Running python mechanism_audit/analyze.py verifies within-set non-rate controls and recomputes ratios, margins, CVs and conditional moment bounds; it does not rerun training. A full-history dump exceeded the sandbox file-size limit and was removed; the manifest and relevant record subset are preserved instead.

The report is independently reviewable and unfinished as mechanism theory. The next decisive evidence is paired train/test and per-seed trajectory instrumentation, not another claim or an invented endpoint.

No identical completed experiment will be repeated. If these observables/interventions remain unavailable, this report will retain the limitation and supply falsifiable future tests rather than invented results.

This is an early, usable publication; analysis and capability audit remain ongoing.

# Same-Architecture Long-Budget Rate Audit
## Evidence and Scope
Read R7dd7d943d3 and K1001/K1002/K1072/K1073 first; later read R7dd7d943d3's completed version at the checkpoint. Its survived repairs and existing experiments were not rerun. Initial frozen inputs: 893 visible training records and 11,366 lab candidates including prior experiments. Initial e0002 inputs remain archived separately. Current K1072 already says multivariate exclusion does NOT establish high-rate safety; that repair was preserved.
The supplied epoch-2 higher/lower-log-Delta counts (multivariate24/5, tabular33/10) motivate this investigation but were not independently reconstructed as a population-bias statistic. Selected failures and outcome-selected dataflip history cannot estimate universal error frequencies.
Nominal Delta is lr*T for Adam-family/RMSprop and 2*lr*sqrt(T) for Adagrad, not measured parameter movement. Ratios below are high-rate mean held-out loss / low-rate mean; margins are high minus low. SDs describe ten training seeds, not paired confidence intervals. No seed-win counts or significance claims are available.

## Training and Lab Audit
q_38909f: dimension2 target x0*x1**2+x0**3+x1**2+.5, uniform [0,1], point seed2085328771, 256 train/256 test rows; T2048, batch16, 32768 sampled rows. Shared default-init nonresidual MLP depth3/width256, LeakyReLU(.01), LN[T,F,T]. B AdamW lr3e-5/wd1e-5/betas(.9,.999) wins; C AdamW lr.001/wd1e-4/betas(.9,.95) loses. Thus this is not a rate-only contrast. A Adagrad lr.003/wd.001 also loses. History supplies no numerical margins.
q_a57013: dimension16 piecewise boundary on x7/x12, breakpoint .5, branch scores 1.125*x12-1.125*x7 and -.875*x12-1.125*x7, threshold0; point seed4000672263957. There are 1024 train/2048 test rows, T512, batch64, 32768 sampled rows: 32 exposure epochs, not 32 exact passes.
Its shared default-init nonresidual depth4/width256 GELU network has LN[T,F,T,F]. Ordinal order A<E<C<B<D: RMSprop(3e-5,wd.001), Adagrad(.0001,wd.001), Adagrad(.003,wd1e-5), AdamW(.0003,wd1e-5,betas .9/.999), SGD(.001,wd0,momentum0). Optimizer and decay confound the adaptive ordering; even E/C changes decay. “Generalization reversal” is a hypothesis, not an observed train/test decomposition.
Visible-history same-architecture/same-optimizer rate comparisons: multivariate higher wins38/45 across28 questions; tabular31/34 across19 questions. Requiring equal displayed optimizer settings except rate gives multivariate4/5 across5 questions, tabular8/10 across10. These include imported visible training records; candidate pairs are dependent and displayed-bullet matching is not proof of equality of hidden runner defaults.
Original lab: zero rate-only pairs/zero sets in these two families when model, initialization, loss, budget and optimizer settings except lr all match within set. Existing R7dd7d943d3 controls use other architectures/recipes and are kept separate.

## Preregistered Experiments
Predictions were saved before each new outcome in preregistration.md: polynomial high-rate wins short/low-rate wins long; deep-GELU Adagrad likewise reverses at E32; polynomial reversal transfers to another polynomial; deep Adagrad high-rate preference transfers to smooth data; RMSprop beats AdamW in a full-recipe analogue; historical sparse/smooth AdamW rate reversal transports to two lab instances.

Within each rate pair, architecture, width, activation, normalization, initialization convention, split, loss, optimizer configuration and budget are fixed. Across budgets, batch stays fixed but T and samples seen change together; their separate causal effects are unidentified. Dataset transfers hold recipe and dimension fixed but change rule/coefficients/features and split seed jointly.
A protocol error is retained: the first polynomial run inherited MSE+L2(lambda .001), not preregistered plain MSE. A separately identified plain-MSE control corrected the loss and slope key. The erroneous run is supplementary, not substituted for the preregistered result. ## Rate-Only Results

Primary rate-only evidence comprises8 comparisons/6 sets; supplementary inherited-loss evidence adds2 comparisons/1 set. Each ratio is a ratio of seed-mean losses, not a mean of paired-seed ratios. Cross-recipe arithmetic averaging is deliberately avoided.

## Full-Recipe and Dataset Reversals
Within exp:ddb38c8f1249, the A architecture on piecewise stabcls_06550f at T512/batch64 gives RMSprop(3e-5,wd.001) CE .291769±.027333; AdamW(.0003,wd1e-5,betas .9/.999) .361090±.038405; Adagrad(.003,wd1e-5) .279363±.034076.
AdamW/RMSprop ratio1.23759, margin+.069321: one comparison/one set transports q_a57013's RMSprop-over-AdamW direction. Higher nominal Delta wins only1/3 optimizer-pair comparisons in this set. This does not identify rate, decay or state as the cause. The preregistered reuse of the slow-Adagrad cell from another experiment is inadmissible under within-set rules; no cross-set E/C loss ratio is used.
Two historical exact-recipe dataset reversals are relevant: q_a9073c/q_07b812, dimension8 residual ReLU depth2/width192 LN[F,T], AdamW(.9,.999), wd1e-5, rates.001/3e-5, T1024/batch32/E32: high rate is selected on sparse data, low on smooth. q_9d6507/q_b9d45e, dimension8 nonresidual ReLU depth1/width192/no LN, RMSprop wd0, rates.001/.0001, same budget: high selected on sparse, low on smooth.
These are2 matched recipe groups/4 question sets, with ordinal outcomes only and unavailable numerical margins. Selection winners establish those pair directions but not complete rankings. Their datasets differ in active features, coefficients and split seeds as well as rule family. The broader36 matched-history groups were outcome-selected dataflip examples, not a reversal prevalence estimate.
Controlled W analogues do NOT reproduce the first reversal: both sparse and smooth favor high rate. The historical counterexamples stand, but their family labels alone do not transport the ordering.

## Interpretation, Tests and Boundaries
Progress limitation is compatible with short-budget high-rate wins; endpoint precision, instability, optimizer-specific trajectories and generalization all remain compatible with long-budget reversals. The high-rate P endpoint can worsen with longer training while low rate improves, but neither training loss nor intermediate trajectories were returned. RMSprop/AdamW contrast is not an isolated optimizer-state intervention. No observed logit, confidence, train/test gap, parameter movement or accumulator measurement establishes a mechanism.
Unrun discriminating tests: log train/test losses through time; falling train loss with rising held-out loss would favor generalization over simple failure to fit. A high-rate phase followed by low-rate continuation should recover endpoint quality if late refinement matters, but must be compared with fixed-rate controls at equal total samples and schedules.
To distinguish optimizer-state effects, compare identical continuation weights/minibatch streams with preserved versus reset state. To distinguish batch from exposure, cross batch16/64 with matched samples and separately matched T. To test stability, collect finite-loss failures and trajectories under clipping. These predictions require additional supported controls; they were not silently implemented using endpoint-only APIs.
No continuous optimum, dimension law, width law, universal epoch cutoff, or population-wide bias mechanism follows. Original q_38909f/q_a57013 splits, alternate initialization, wider seed cohorts, intermediate rates and independent split replication remain untested.

## KB and Reproducibility
Submitted3 new scoped claims (tool returned K1078/K1079/K1080) and annotations to K1001, K1002 and K1073. They record exact polynomial rate/budget results, the failed low-Adagrad E32 prediction, and the full-recipe RMSprop/AdamW contrast. No stale K1072 safety repair was repeated, and no universal rate ceiling was proposed.
The repo preserves initial frozen_inputs.json, checkpoint_inputs.json, lab_snapshot.json, new_experiments.json, preregistration.md, proposed_changes.json and exact set/candidate IDs. Run python analyze.py and python analyze_history.py to recompute numerical pairs and ordinal audits. The scripts were executed successfully in the allowed Python sandbox. New experiments comprise23 variants/8 sets; resolved recipes, dataset cards, measurement sources, SDs and preregistration reasons are archived.
Exact primary sets: exp:630c92c3db03, exp:ab716597e66e, exp:e0f4b22f48fd, exp:4f26a5846f00, exp:502abb610bf2, exp:f5533b6425ee. Supplementary inherited loss: exp:585913a8fe26; full recipes: exp:ddb38c8f1249. Training reruns require the lab runner; local scripts reproduce analysis, not an independently reimplemented trainer.
This report is independently reviewable but unfinished as a mechanism theory. Same-split/config/seed recomputation can falsify its numerical statements; new datasets or seed cohorts test extrapolation, not erase the recorded comparisons.

## Preregistration and Controls
Predictions were recorded before outcomes: polynomial high-rate wins short/low-rate wins long; deep-GELU Adagrad likewise reverses at 32 exposure epochs; polynomial reversal transfers to another polynomial; historical sparse/smooth AdamW reversal transfers to lab analogues; RMSprop beats AdamW in a full-recipe tabular analogue.

Each rate pair fixes dataset, architecture, width, normalization, initialization convention, loss, optimizer configuration and budget. All runs start fresh. Across budgets, batch remains fixed but T and samples seen change together: their separate effects are unidentified.

A protocol error is preserved: the first polynomial experiment inherited MSE+L2(.001), rather than preregistered plain MSE. A separately identified plain-MSE control corrected this. The inherited-loss results are supplementary, not substituted for the intended test.

Unspecified optimizer knobs use runner defaults; optimizer-state trajectories were not independently measured.

## Rate-Only Results

Targets are `x0**3+x0*x1+x1−2` and `x0*x1**2+x1**3+x0`, each with 256/256 uniform points. At T2048, Δ=.06144 versus2.048. Both support the preregistered direction; the second high-rate SD exceeds its mean, making its large ratio particularly seed-sensitive.

**Adagrad counterexample:** higher rate wins **3/3 comparisons across2 sets**, including **2/2 at 32 exposure epochs**. The predicted lower-rate reversal failed. The smooth margin is small relative to seed variability. These results reject a blanket low-Adagrad-rate rule, but do not test safety at Δ≥.5.

**AdamW transfer failure:** higher rate wins **2/2 comparisons across2 sets**, both at 32 exposure epochs, with Δ=.03072 versus1.024. The predicted sparse/smooth dataset reversal failed. A smooth dataset can therefore favor Δ>1 under this exact residual recipe.

Primary rate-only evidence comprises **8 comparisons/6 sets**; supplementary inherited-loss evidence adds **2 comparisons/1 set**. Cross-recipe averages are deliberately avoided.

## Full-Recipe and Dataset Reversals
Within `exp:ddb38c8f1249`, the deep-GELU architecture on piecewise `stabcls_06550f`, T512/batch64, gives:
- RMSprop(3e-5,wd.001): CE **.291769±.027333**.
- AdamW(.0003,wd1e-5,betas .9/.999): **.361090±.038405**.
- Adagrad(.003,wd1e-5): **.279363±.034076**.

AdamW/RMSprop ratio is **1.23759**, margin **+.069321**, from **1 comparison/1 set**. This transports one full-recipe reversal from q_a57013, without identifying rate, decay or optimizer state as its cause. Higher nominal Δ wins only **1/3 optimizer-pair comparisons** in this set.

The preregistered reuse of a slow-Adagrad cell from another experiment is inadmissible under within-set comparison rules; no cross-set E/C numerical ratio is used.

Two exact-recipe historical dataset reversals remain relevant:
- **q_a9073c/q_07b812:** dimension8 residual ReLU depth2/width192, LN `[F,T]`, AdamW, rates.001/3e-5, T1024/batch32. Higher wins sparse; lower wins smooth.
- **q_9d6507/q_b9d45e:** dimension8 nonresidual ReLU depth1/width192, no LN, RMSprop wd0, rates.001/.0001, same budget. Higher wins sparse; lower wins smooth.

These are **2 matched recipe groups/4 question sets**, with ordinal outcomes and unavailable numerical margins. Rule family, active features, coefficients and split seeds change jointly. Controlled W analogues do not reproduce the first reversal: both favor higher rate. Historical counterexamples stand, but family labels alone do not transport their ordering.

## Interpretation and Unresolved Tests
Short-budget high-rate wins are compatible with progress limitation. Long-budget reversals remain compatible with late precision, instability, optimizer-specific trajectories or generalization. Endpoint losses alone distinguish none of these mechanisms.

Discriminating tests remain unrun: collect training/test trajectories; compare high-to-low schedules against fixed-rate controls at equal samples; compare continuation with preserved versus reset optimizer state; cross batch sizes under separately matched T and samples; measure finite-loss failures and clipping responses. Falling training loss with rising test loss would favor generalization over failure to fit.

No continuous optimum, universal epoch cutoff, dimension/width law or population-wide bias mechanism follows. Original question splits, alternative initializations, independent seed cohorts and intermediate rates remain untested. Multivariate exclusion from univariate overshoot is not evidence of high-rate safety.

## Publication and Reproducibility
Submitted **3 scoped claims** and annotations to K1001, K1002 and K1073. No existing K1072 safety repair was repeated and no universal ceiling was proposed.

Published **Rc5401dd3c0**, commit **1e459f265c35bb1e2ef32bb4a161b0a85ee538d3**. The repo preserves frozen inputs, checkpoint inputs, lab snapshots, resolved experiments, preregistrations, proposed changes and exact measurement sources. `python analyze.py` and `python analyze_history.py` successfully recompute numerical and ordinal audits. New experiments comprise **23 variants/8 sets**; training reruns require the lab runner.

This report is independently reviewable, but unfinished as a mechanism theory.

Initial checkpoint; intentionally unfinished. Inputs: frozen epoch-2 visible training history (893 records), current KB, R7dd7d943d3 and allowed lab (11366 candidates including experiments). No evaluation answers used. R7dd7d943d3's surviving repairs will not be repeated.

# Sparse-interaction depth1–3 audit at AdamW Δ=.0768 and 16 epochs

## Scope and definitions
Frozen inputs: 953 history records, load_kb(), base load_lab(False), q_879733, q_f67653, K1009/K1033/K1056 and report R04f88f629b. History supplies ten-seed mean-loss rankings, not numerical losses. Lab supplies ten-seed mean test CE and seed SD; compare only within one set_id. Depth counts hidden width-to-width blocks, excluding input projection and output head. Normalization is pre-linear in each block, residual addition precedes activation. Δ=lr*T for AdamW is a proxy, not measured parameter displacement. T256 batch64 on 1024 train rows means 16384 sampled presentations, or 16 nominal epochs with replacement.

## Exact focal records
Both use iid standard-normal eight-feature input, deterministic binary labels, 1024 train/2048 test rows, CPU, cross entropy, PyTorch Linear default initialization, seeds 0–9, T256 batch64, AdamW lr=.0003, Δ=.0768.
q_879733: s=1.25*x1*x4-.875*x1*x5-1.25*x2*x5; threshold0; point seed712964138, calibration712965138; calibration positive51.1%. Betas(.9,.999), decay1e-5. Recipes (depth,width,residual,activation,LN mask): A=(3,64,true,LeakyReLU .01,[T,T,T]); B=(1,128,true,LeakyReLU .01,[T]); C=(1,128,false,SiLU,[F]); D=(2,96,false,SiLU,[F,T]); E=(2,96,true,ReLU,[F,T]). Gold D<E<A<B<C, prediction D<B<A<E<C. E and A beat B, but E beats A: no monotone depth law.
q_f67653: s=-1.125*x4*x6-1.125*x4*x7+1.25*x2*x6; threshold0; point seed2264868794, calibration2264869794; calibration positive48.6%. Betas(.9,.95), decay1e-4. A=(2,128,true,SiLU,[T,F]); B=(2,128,false,LeakyReLU .01,[F,F]); C=(2,96,true,GELU,[F,F]); D=(3,96,false,ReLU,[F,F,F]); E=(1,128,true,SiLU,[F]). Gold A<B<D<C<E, prediction A<C<E<B<D. Normalized smooth A wins; the remaining rectifier/plain versus smooth/residual comparisons do not isolate activation.

## Count audit (interim)
audit.py and audit_core.json/audit_linear.json preserve exact filters and candidate pairs; source snapshots are saved. Require same optimizer type/lr and budget, plain CE lab, nonexcluded candidates, and both residual with at least one LN for depth. For Δ .03–.1, exclude focal q_879733 and restrict both depths1–3: deeper wins2/4 across2 questions: q_062cad A–B and A–E both lose; q_546d0f A–C and D–C both win. This reconstructs 2/4, but pools datasets, budgets and architectures, not the focal optimizer condition.
The unrestricted normalized-residual lab audit gives2/6 deeper wins across6 sets, NOT4/6. Under lr*T for all adaptive optimizers, shallower wins4/6 and there is one sparse-interaction pair; core-calibrated Adagrad instead gives2/6 deeper with3 sparse pairs. Hence the comment’s deeper4/6 cannot currently be validated and must not be used as measured support. Full details and effects will follow.
q_f67653 has4 zero-LN plain-rectifier/smooth-residual pair wins in one question. Equal-width restriction gives2/2 (B–E and D–C), plausibly reconstructing its comment’s2 historical pairs; no independent historical question satisfies the filter. Zero corresponding base-lab matches. Equal-LN sparse lab broadening gives0/2 rectifier wins across2 sets, but is not zero-LN or an activation-only test.
K1009 pools separate shallow/smooth/LN preferences with data-rule and budget gates; K1056 calls smoothness only a tendency below .1. K1033’s principal controlled evidence is 16-input depth2vs4 at T512 batch64, 32 epochs, Adam/Adagrad, not this eight-input depth1vs3 AdamW condition. R04f88f629b explicitly warns about pooled architectural and optimizer confounding.

## Preregistered single contrast
Choose only q_879733 A vs B: normalized residual LeakyReLU(.01) depth3 width64 mask[T,T,T] versus depth1 width128 mask[T], using AdamW lr.0003 betas(.9,.999), decay1e-5, default init, CE, T256/batch64, seeds0–9. This fixes two complete recipes, not parameter count or width; no other contrast will be trained.
Prediction before measurement: A has lower mean test CE than B on each of stabcls_0db74c and stabcls_17011f. Record signed A-minus-B CE and A/B ratio even on reversal. Selection is two allowed eight-feature sparse datasets, not selection by this contrast’s measured outcome.
Dataset1: point33093035, instance33092035, s=1.5*x1*x7-1*x3*x4+1.375*x4*x7. Dataset2: point145093376, instance145092376, s=-1.375*x1*x4+1.125*x4*x6+.875*x4*x5. Both threshold0, 1024/2048 rows. Saved dataset cards specify exact generator.
All persisted experiment rows inspected: only two prior sparse rows on dataset1, depth2 width192 ReLU residual [F,T], T1024/batch32 at lr3e-5/.001. They do not match either new recipe. Never repeat persisted experiments; exact config signatures will be checked before launch.

## Uncertainty, alternatives and boundaries
Recipe generalization across targets is testable here; slower unnormalized smooth feature learning and distractor overfit are competing unmeasured explanations, not established mechanisms. A reversal falsifies the predicted recipe transfer. Train/test trajectories and factorial width/depth/LN tests could distinguish alternatives, but are not part of this single-contrast experiment. Seed covariance is unavailable, so aggregate SDs cannot yield paired significance. Two datasets are not a population-wide generalization result.
This usable interim report is published before experiments/mechanism completion. No parent claims rewritten; at most one new condition-first claim will be considered after results.

## 问题与定义

此前三份报告只比较终点均值。现在核查：优势是否由大多数种子支持，是否在训练中途反转，失败种子有没有被均值遗漏，以及执行配方是否符合报告。只读取允许训练实验库的六组实验；没有读取 benchmark val/test 题或重跑训练。曲线中的“test”指各训练实验自带的测试划分。

MSE为均方误差，CE为交叉熵，越低越好。差值为前者−后者；负值表示前者更好。每格有相同编号0–9的十个随机数生成器种子（RNG seed）。配对标准误SE=差值的样本标准差/√10；±是SE，不是置信区间。种子胜数统计同编号终点损失的大小，不等于跨数据集胜率。

## 曲线中的反转

这是T2048原有训练路径的前缀，不是新增T256/T512/T1024独立训练。每步测试metric保存在curves.npz：回归/螺旋末步2048、samples32768、batch16；稀疏末步256、samples16384、batch64。

| 高−低率MSE差值 | 第256步 | 第512步 | 第1024步 | 第2048步 |

| mvar_0eb811, beta2=.999 | +0.055057186 | +0.060117424 | -0.087452161 | -0.22391917 |

高率并非全程更好：beta2=.999的两数据从第817/543步起持续更好；beta2=.95从470/503步起持续更好。这里“持续”是记录内最后一次方向切换后到2048步，属于事后描述，不是预测的临界步。高率早期更差、长预算反超，与旧多项式高率早期好而后期落后的方向相反。

螺旋同d3/FTF的残差在第64和128步都是10/10种子更好，到第256及2048步反而0/10更好；均值plain优势从176/178步起持续。d2/TT从279/284步起plain持续更好。middle对terminal LN早期较差，后从361/314步起较好；first对middle LN只在前6/5步占均值优势。SiLU对Leaky(.1)的TFF比较均值全程较差。稀疏A初始较差，但第15/21步后持续优于B，优势在128步比终点更大。

图示使用已保存的十种子平均曲线，纵轴对数；无梯度、特征尺度或训练损失信息。

![已记录的测试曲线反转](recorded-reversals.png)

## 竞争解释（均待验证）

回归可能涉及优化速度、不同轨迹/局部解、更新噪声或率相关的累计衰减。固定AdamW wd系数并不固定累计收缩；仅凭高率后期测试误差下降，不能证明大位移、泛化或beta记忆机制。多项式与嵌套目标还同时改变数据划分，不能把相反反转归因于表达式复杂度。

螺旋可由skip改变优化动力学、LN位置改变特征尺度、初始化或跨层组合解释。训练过程确实有快慢翻转，但没有train loss、梯度、update范数或feature统计，无法识别中介机制；实际slope=.1还限制了与原题的联系。稀疏全配方的优势可能来自归一化、组合深度或宽度优化，当前对照没有单独识别任何因素。

## 可区分预测（未执行）

先在新训练数据划分固定执行配方并预注册反转方向；若低→高率长预算反超或残差早期快/晚期慢不再出现，就收窄数据适用域。螺旋还需明确slope=.01与.1的匹配对照，检验现有结论能否转回原题设置。

测量逐种子train/test轨迹及gradient/update/feature尺度，能分开训练拟合滞后与训练好、测试坏。若低率train更差且降率/升率续训同时恢复train/test，支持优化限制；若train持续好而test转坏，才支持泛化解释。

在相同checkpoint、相同后续批次下保留/重置Adam状态并改变beta2或rate，可检验记忆与噪声解释；稀疏需要固定width/LN/depth的factorial对照。以上需要新接口和新实验，本次未执行，也未提出已成立理论。

## 边界与复现

同编号种子只足以报告“配对RNG种子”。train.py从torch.manual_seed(seed)开始，先构建模型，再用同全局RNG的torch.randint取batch。回归对照的model.py/train.py完整字节相同，按代码预期共享初始形状和随机流；没有实际初始tensor或batch哈希可独立证明。改变宽度/深度会改变构模消耗，稀疏因此不能称为相同初始权重/批次。当前环境deterministic_algorithms=false、CPU单线程、Gitcommit=null；执行文件已保留hash但未获得运行时tensor证据。

每格十个seed只重采样初始化/训练随机性，不是十个独立数据集。六个已选允许数据集、每主题两个，不能估计总体外推概率。没有训练损失、checkpoint分叉、state重置或过程尺度；不推断校准、独立benchmark涨分和梯度机理。

所有来源、spec/summary/curves和model/train/loss/optimizer字节保存在evidence/，源路径及SHA256在manifest.json；dataset训练/测试文件只记录路径/完整哈希。运行 `python audit.py` 即可只用冻结证据重算analysis.json、curve-checkpoints.csv及图；`--freeze`是显式重新复制来源，默认不读取现场实验。报告pin和原receipt也在sources/。完整复制及解析哈希已验证，analysis.json含全部22个配对对照和逐种子差值。

# Initial-Scale versus Normalization Geometry

## Status and Sources
Ongoing preregistered investigation; no new training outcomes yet. Read R04f88f629b, R838be7703a and current repaired KB. Frozen inputs: 983 history records, 11,601 lab candidates. Compressed inputs saved in scale_audit/. The requested deferred job has no matching visible history record; its report lookup returned unrelated prior reports, not identifiable new evidence. Do not reapply obsolete repairs. Existing parity and spiral controls will not be duplicated.

## Definitions
Depth counts hidden blocks; terminal LN means last hidden block normalized, not greatest LN count. Old K1059 pairs are nonresidual depth>=2 same nominal SGD or adaptive optimizer; width/depth/activation and full optimizer equality are not guaranteed. Old K1038 contrasts deep smooth zeroLN SGD with adaptive at calibrated SGD Delta>=3*rival, rival Delta<.1; preserve residual and family. New controls fix width24, SiLU, default init, batch16,T256,wd0; cross depth2/4/5, plain/residual, zero/one-early/one-terminal/all LN and optimizer. Early versus terminal holds count at one. SGD m0 lr.003; SGD m.9 lr.0003; Adam(.9,.999) lr.00003. CE Delta=.00768 in all three; MSE momentum calibration=.02304, others=.00768. These proxies are not actual matched motion.

## Predictions before Measurement
On two allowed metadata-matched splits per family, terminalLN will beat one-earlyLN more consistently for deep plain SGD than Adam. Residuals should reduce the plain deep zeroLN deficit; no prediction that residual always wins terminalLN or MSE. Deep plain zeroLN should have lower input-dependent head feature scale and gradient RMS than d2; raw RMS alone may include bias and is insufficient. A fixed nonnormalizing scalar calibrated on training inputs to restore terminalLN head RMS should recover much of the SGD terminalLN advantage if scalar shrinkage is sufficient. If it restores RMS but not sensitivity, gradients, updates or loss, pure scalar shrinkage is rejected. LN centers and projects its Jacobian; normalization geometry can remain decisive. Adam may be less sensitive to scalar attenuation, but epsilon, head logits and nonlinear trajectories prevent exact scale invariance.

## Method and Limitations
Compare held-out losses only within set_id. Preserve means, SDs, failures, dependent pair counts and source IDs; do not infer seed significance from summary SD. Audit old counts separately from new causal controls. Measure head raw/centered RMS, input sensitivity, per-layer gradient RMS, optimizer update RMS, step0 CE/MSE and final LN gain only if a faithful executable measurement route is available. Endpoint tool alone cannot measure these. Allowed datasets only. No unsupported frozen label or universal ranking. Finish means independently reviewable evidence and explicit missing tests, not a finished mechanism theory.

# Initial-Scale versus LayerNorm Geometry

## Interim Answer
Initial feature/gradient scale remains an unmeasured candidate, not a demonstrated explanation. Terminal placement has matched endpoint effects, but residual and family strata already prevent a universal placement or LN-count score. The experiment interface cannot instrument internals or scalar-tail rescue. Report is usable but mechanism unfinished.

## Inputs and Definitions
Read R04f88f629b/R838be7703a and repaired KB. Frozen 983 history records/11,601 lab candidates saved compressed. Deferred J290340c95a93:000005 is absent from visible history; report lookup is nondiagnostic, so no obsolete repair is repeated. Supplied negative utilities are motivation, not reconstructable exposure statistics.

Generated block code is PRE-LN: plain SiLU(Linear(LN(x))), residual SiLU(x+Linear(LN(x))). Depth counts these blocks after a separate projection/SiLU. TerminalLN means LN before the last block's linear, NOT a unit-RMS head input. Bias and activation after LN can change head RMS. AllLN normalizes every block input, zeroLN none; early versus terminal each has one LN.

Old K1059 reports SGD31/31 across14sets,CE ratio.69 and Adam70/102,.92. Original selection filter is underidentified. Explicit nonexcluded base-lab/plainCE/nonresidual d>=2/within-set/same optimizer type gives SGD36/52,.981824 and Adam27/70,1.051067. Adding equal lr gives5/5,.965316 and6/12,1.024390; adding full optimizer equality gives0 SGD pairs and Adam2/3,.763836. Width/depth/activation remain unmatched. These are different definitions, not interchangeable replications.

Old K1038 reproduces exactly under nonexcluded/base-lab/plainMSE-or-CE,SGD deep>=3 SiLU/GELU zeroLN,SGD calibratedDelta>=3*rival and rivalDelta<.1:11/30 in11sets,medianSGD/rival1.055903. Plain3/15 in5sets,1.896676;residual8/15 in6sets,.991373. Multivariate3/11,1.698466;univariate2/10,1.607376;spiral4/5,.968989;XOR2/4,.995387. Normalized>=1LN413/471 in171sets,.577774. No terminal-placement or exact-model match is imposed here. These rows coexist in one table but cannot be pooled with terminal placement pairs.

## Preregistered Controls
Width24/defaultinit/SiLU/wd0/batch16/T256 on two metadata-identical allowed point splits per family: XOR063fc1/4779bd,tabular sparse-interaction168586/ffe3ff,1.5-turn spiral00f3c5/01a657,MSE0e8d19/d2b5db with identical x0**3+x0*x1+sin(2*pi*x1) target. SGD0 lr.003;SGD.9 lr.0003;Adam(.9,.999)lr3e-5. CE calibratedDelta=.00768 each;MSE momentum=.02304 versus.00768. These proxies do not imply matched actual updates.

Predictions published before outcomes: deep plain SGD terminal beats one-early more consistently/strongly than Adam; residual reduces deep zeroLN deficit without a universal skip or MSE preference. Planned allLN and d5 controls remain pending; d2 adaptive placement is not yet measured. Every contrast must be within its experiment set; repeated cached anchors are not new replications.

## Interim Results and Failures
Completed120 unique configurations/1,200 new seed evaluations,0 failed seeds;122 returned rows include2 cached repeats. Full configurations,seed outcomes,generated recipes and within-set contrasts are saved. Paired95% t9 intervals use seed differences; no multiplicity correction or population reliability inference.

Plain SGD0 terminal/early wins12/12 classification cells across six splits at d2/d4; these are not12 independent datasets. Ratios at d4 are XOR.999143/.997851,tabular.995975/.995270,spiral.978157/.980805. At d2 ratios are appreciably lower. Residual spiral d2 reverses placement on both splits: terminal/early1.003894/1.004266;d4 favors terminal. MSE residual terminal/early loses at both depths on both splits,while plain terminal wins. Negative-control MSE therefore does not support a universal terminal effect.

On the two measured XOR d4 plain Adam cells terminal wins2/2,ratios.996382/.996072,versus plain SGD0 .999143/.997851. The stronger-SGD relative-effect prediction fails descriptively on these splits; both gains remain small. Remaining optimizer/family replays and allLN/d5 controls are ongoing.

## Mechanism and Measurement Boundary
Sandbox torch import fails with blocked ctypes.dlopen. Allowed pool contains specs/summaries but no exported point arrays or initial states; inventing a NumPy seed replay would not be faithful. Head raw/centered RMS,input sensitivity,layer gradient RMS,actual updates,step0 CE/MSE,learned gain and fixed scalar-tail rescue are UNMEASURED. No freeze claim follows from CE nearln2.

LN changes both scale and geometry: its Jacobian removes the feature-mean direction and approximately the radial direction, with epsilon corrections. A scalar preserves these directions and ratios of centered sensitivity to RMS. Required future discriminator: calibrate scalar on training inputs only to restore terminal head RMS without LN; hold weights/minibatches/optimizer fixed,measure scale,sensitivity,gradient/update trajectories and gain. Rescue of RMS without optimization or loss rescue refutes scalar sufficiency,not every scale contribution. Head-logit calibration,centered information,normalization geometry,skip/SiLU composition and optimizer state remain alternatives.

## Solver and Reproduction
Condition first: identify loss family,optimizer full recipe,depth/residual status and actual LN placement. Use matched lowDelta placement evidence for its measured recipe; preserve spiral/MSE residual reversals. Do not sum LN+residual units,force cross-activation/depth ranking,import the MSE momentum calibration into within-SGD parity,or call zeroLN frozen. K1101 parity,K1108 adaptive mixed-recipe andK1109 offset-MSE counterexamples remain intact.

Run python scale_audit/analyze.py to reproduce exact old counts and all new within-set contrasts. Compressed frozen inputs,old_pairs.json,experiments/*.json,recipes/,contrasts.json andregime_table.csv/json preserve measurement sources. Initial snapshot write exceeded16MiB; compressed replacement succeeded. The earlier missing-gzip import failed without modifying measurements and was corrected in the saved analyzer. No new KB claim has yet been submitted; this continuing report will update after the remaining evidence and checkpoint.

Hard relative benefit strengthens from T256 to2048 on both new splits;this does not prove a universal late-training trend.0717d7's T256 margin is much smaller than C's SD;without paired covariance no confidence or reliable seedwise win rate is claimed. Separately,rate-only A/C factorials with wd0 and matched optimizer would test whether >=3x rate suffices;decay-only C controls would test the easy-loss account. Those are future tests,not measured claims.
The broader rule remains sparsely supported beyond this exact d3w256/all-LN bundle. No extension to all2turn datasets,all smooth/rectifier activations,other rates,architectures,budgets or seed populations is established.

recipe_audit contains archived history/kb/lab,checkpoint,preregistration,base/history pair tables,24 experiment rows,results,reproduce.py and summarize.py. Run python recipe_audit/reproduce.py then python recipe_audit/summarize.py;full-precision means/SD/margins/ratios and dataset/initialization provenance are preserved. Two condition-first empirical KB claims are proposed,each under700 characters. This complete ongoing report preserves counterexamples and unresolved questions rather than asserting finished theory.

Endpoint bundle ranking may predict recipe utility without proving a mechanism. # Adam-family full-recipe spiral transfer

## Findings
**The historical comparison reverses, and the original recipe reversal transfers at T2048.** Byte-identical choice sections favor A on one turn (`q_fe080b`) and C on three turns (`q_b3f618`). New experiments favor A on both one-turn datasets and C on both three-turn datasets at T2048.

The residual rectifier recipe also beats the plain smooth recipe on both three-turn datasets at T256. This supports the **specific full recipe**, not a universal ≥3× learning-rate preference, residual advantage, or causal turns cutoff.

## Inputs and Historical Gold
Read K1020/K1040/K1066/K1070/K1096–1099 and reports R1dd74ea5c0/R2ffac818b0 before experiments. Initial inputs contained 923 history records and 59 claims; checkpoint refresh pinned `J4e869fe335b4_research_e0003`.

`q_fe080b`: dataflip500, epoch −996, one turn, point seed1236348397, gold A.  
`q_b3f618`: dataflip500, epoch3, three turns, point seed1236356316, gold C.

Both use T2048, batch16, 32768 samples, train1024/test2048, CPU, default PyTorch initialization, and ten seeds0–9. Historical gold is ordinal: numerical margins and the complete three-choice ordering are unavailable.

|Recipe|Architecture|Optimizer|
|---|---|---|
|A|plain d3w256 SiLU, LN[1,1,1]|AdamW .0003, betas(.9,.95), wd0|
|B|plain d4w192 GELU, LN[0,0,0,1]|Adagrad .0001, wd0|
|C|residual d3w256 ReLU, LN[1,1,1]|Adam .001, betas(.9,.95), wd.001|

A/C match depth, width, LN placement, betas and budget. Activation, skips, optimizer type, 3.333× rate and coupled decay remain bundled. Across questions, turns, point seed and coordinate radius change together. B additionally changes depth, width, normalization and optimizer family.

## Rule Audit
Excluding focal q_b3f618, eligibility required residual ReLU/LeakyReLU versus plain SiLU/GELU, Adam/AdamW, at least equal depth/LN count, ≥3× rate, and equal budget within T256–2048.

The stated counts reproduce:
- **History broad3/4**, with q_fe080b the counterexample; restricting to2–3 turns gives **1/1**, at2.5 turns/T512.
- **Base lab broad4/4**; hard2/2 gives CE ratios **.914047/.992245**, both T256.
- No qualifying prior **long-budget hard-spiral lab pair** exists in the archived inputs.

These are pairwise bundle comparisons. Equal LN counts need not mean equal placement; they do not isolate a learning-rate mechanism.

## Preregistration and Methods
Published the initial report before experiments. Selected the first two lexicographic allowed splits at each of one and three turns, without inspecting new outcomes. Tested original A/B/C at T256 and T2048, batch16, keeping budgets and easy/hard data separate.

Predicted C over A on both hard splits at both budgets, A over C on easy splits at T2048, and B worse throughout. Exploratory easy-T256 prediction favored C. Existing d4w24 LeakyReLU optimizer and equal-LN d5SiLU/d3ReLU controls were **not repeated**.

Point seeds:05d021=100035085215;06bcc2=48093085;0717d7=100069017411;0cfa0b=150198009. All splits have train1024/test2048. Initialization is recorded as default; individual lab seed streams are not exposed.

## Results

|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|

B loses all eight conditions. Its full means/SDs are saved with the other results. The exploratory easy-T256 prediction **fails on06bcc2**.

Four experiment sets contain24 configurations and240 scheduled seed runs. All24 returned finite mean/SD summaries and `error=null`; per-seed finite counts and failed-seed counts are unavailable, so240 verified finite runs are not asserted. An invalid `name` override was rejected before training and then removed.

## Uncertainty and Boundaries
The first hard-T256 margin is small relative to C’s SD. Paired losses/covariance are unavailable; no significance or seedwise win-rate claim follows. Large easy SDs indicate seed-tail sensitivity. Numerically zero A losses require absolute margins, not finite ratios or claims of zero population risk.

The persisted schema retains inherited `lambda10` alongside `loss_id=cross_entropy`. Plain CE was explicitly selected, but implementation-level historical equivalence cannot be independently inspected here.

Faster fitting, decay-limited tiny easy losses, activation/LN interactions, optimizer dynamics and coordinate scaling remain competing explanations. Endpoint CE distinguishes recipe rankings, not these mechanisms.

Unmeasured predictions: a third allowed three-turn split should favor C at both budgets; a third one-turn split should favor A at T2048. Opposite signs reject transfer. Matched optimizer/rate/decay factorials would test whether rate or decay explains the bundle advantage. No extension to all two-turn datasets, activations, architectures or budgets is established.

## Reproducibility and Publication
`recipe_audit/` preserves frozen inputs, checkpoint, preregistration, qualifying pairs, experiment rows, full-precision means/SDs/margins/ratios, provenance and analysis scripts. Run `reproduce.py` and `summarize.py`.

Published **Rfd410c853b**, commit `42d767021d1e5c049ab6dcf88c0ab6f81e52c0e7`. Submitted exactly two condition-first claims, **K1100/K1101**, each under700 characters. Failed transfers and unresolved questions remain explicit.
