snaps.render:
[K1001] For shared-model/data/budget optimizer comparisons BELOW task-specific saturation, use cumulative displacement Δ as a progress proxy, not a universal test-loss ranking. Check K1004/K1071-K1073 before choosing maximum Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T; Adagrad: 2·lr·√T; SGD: lr·T·|g|/(1-m), |g|≈0.01 (bigram 0.003; momentum MSE 0.03, K1019). Older backtests favored larger Δ in ~85% after ceiling exceptions, but not every 256-2048-step task is under-trained. Across different architectures or optimizers, close Δ estimates are not decisive (K1012); use scoped architecture rules. Long-budget spiral/XOR maxima can lose (q_fb4a7f/q_46d72e); no validated general ceiling yet.
[K1002] Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW on the SAME architecture/budget: Adagrad Δ≈2·lr·√T, so comparable progress needs lr≈√T/2 (8-23×) higher. At lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3, Adam-family wins65/70; ratio10 is mixed4/7; ratio≥30 Adagrad wins9/9. For shared-architecture Adagrad rate comparisons, larger lr usually wins (original40/41; broader univariate lab73/78, history13/16), not always; lr3e-3 is not a universal safety guarantee. Do not use this rate preference to settle LN/activation changes (q_cd8a07). At lr≤1e-4, Δ≤0.01 over T≤2048 indicates little progress relative to adaptive rates≥3e-5, but freezing is approximate.
[K1003] Normalized MLPs or bigram LMs,SGD vs adaptive BELOW saturation: plain SGD is often slow,NOT automatically frozen or last. It lost138/141 pairs when adaptiveDelta>15x its estimate(K1019); old all-family appearance wins~8% are pooled,not same-model controls. Momentum.9 lr.001-.003 is a contender,not guaranteed winner: general Adam-equivalent rate~lr/10,bigram~lr/30,MSE~lr/3. At lr<=.0003 it usually loses to same-lr adaptive below saturation. Calibration is a proxy,NOT proof momentum beats plain at equal lr/(1-m);q_0a12ba favors plain at parity,with decay differing. Deep zeroLN smooth MLPs need task-specific scope(K1038).
[K1004] LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. MSE RMSprop lr≥1e-3: versus ≥3× smaller Δ, wins22/36 corpus (better MLP6/6, equal12/22, worse4/8); at equal lr prefer Adam (RMSprop3e-3 loses33/35). Univariate lower-RMSprop-rate preference can occur even below this ceiling (K1063). Bigram optima depend on model width (K1071); wide multilayer univariate high-Δ fitting risk is comparative, not automatic last place (K1072). Tabular optimum changes with epochs/data rule (K1073). Short-budget XOR/spiral often benefit from high rates, but T2048 winners q_46d72e/q_fb4a7f refute blanket long-budget safety; no general replacement ceiling is validated.
[K1005] Shared-model optimizer comparisons BELOW saturation: minor decay/beta differences are weak tie-breakers,not universal noise; a clear undertraining gap usually matters more. Older same-arch higher-wd3/13,all loss gaps<1%;equal-lr Adam/AdamW5/10,beta2.95vs.9997/11. Do NOT assume those knobs are harmless in converged CE or long-budget recipes. Matched easy-spiral controls show coupled-Adam decay penalties atwd>=.001 AND wd1e-4(K1040);different lr/net recipes cannot be ranked from decay alone. q_a57013 at32epochs and q_38909f atT2048 change rate/betas/decay together;their gold does not isolate a 'minor knob' cause or justify blindly maximizing Delta.
[K1006] MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T,lowDelta: LN count is task-specific evidence,NOT LN+residual scoring or a deterministic rank. Older moreLN corpus:multivariate61/72,univariate57/69,tabular41/45;not factor-isolated. Multivariate plain+1LN vsres(K1076):mixed lab23/31,median MSE ratio.906;matched type/lr4/6,no full-config pairs;plain+1depth4/9(ratio1.166) opposes it. Equal-LN regression rectifier evidence(K1008) is not a forced tie-break across residual/tail differences. Regression depth:K1074;multivariate limit:K1080;SGD:K1039;spiral:K1020/K1066;plain tails:K1061(SGD strongest);XOR:K1018/K1065;tabular:K1009/K1033. No universal scoring formula.
[K1008] MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).
[K1009] Tabular CE,1024 rows,shared optimizer/lr/T,Delta>=.1: shallow and smooth are separate preferences; fewer-LN depends on data rule/budget. Old corpus: shallow21/26,smooth16/16; width not isolated. Base-lab moreLN wins: piecewise9/17 (17sets,CE ratio.987),smooth_additive5/13 (11sets,1.196),sparse_interaction0/10 (5sets,1.495). Same optimizer type/lr, but mixed architecture/decay; T256,4096/8192samples,NOT32epochs. Below .1 old moreLN41/45,deeper35/52; 32-epoch depth reversal can start near .03(K1033). Optimizer optima:K1073; activation:K1056. Do not discard residual+LN solely for smoothness or width(q_11a5f0); no universal additive score.
[K1012] For mixed choices, close cross-optimizer Δ estimates are uncertain; a 25% edge is not decisive (q_77d140). BELOW task/model saturation, ≥4× Δ favors progress over architecture (higher wins35/40 even against ≥2 extra LN/residual). Within ~3×, better architecture wins11/19: a weak preference, not a deterministic rank. Once both Δ≳0.3 extra Δ wins only≈62%; check K1004/K1063/K1071-K1073 and data/budget before sorting by Δ. Near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2/lnV, MSE≈Var(y)) are a tied bottom group; use architecture rather than tiny rate differences. No universal RMSprop-over-Adagrad correction is validated for near-parity LM comparisons.
[K1015] MLP residual/depth at shared optimizer/lr/T: residual status is NOT a task-wide trump card. Older confounded corpus: deeper plain regression beats shallower residual24/39; classification deeper residual beats shallow plain33/47,shallow residual beats deep plain19/32. These counts do not isolate skips or justify 'never choose deep plain'. Terminal LN,activation,features and budget matter:K1061,K1065,K1033,K1074. q_6e56f3 at32epochs favors3-block plain over5-block residual; q_611798/q_bca005 reverse identical recipes across1/2-turn datasets. Deep residual appearance53% vs plain29% is not a matched comparison or universal residual+depth rank.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).
[K1017] Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model, layer count: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 FEWER layers wins 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a); Δ≥0.5 fewer 8/11; 0.02≤Δ<0.1 COIN FLIP (fewer 8/15; q_4f69f2, q_9344eb: 2-layer beat 1-layer) - do not decide by depth there; Δ<0.02 deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE - wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 smaller wins 5/6, order by d_model ascending then layers (q_17f213; K1068). GRU vs transformer: K1075; lr: K1071.
[K1018] XOR CE,1024 rows,>=8 features,shared Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr/T,Delta>=.05: smooth is favored (older lab15/16, CE ratio.78; corpus6/6), but fewer LN is NOT validated. Fixed width24 depth2 plain GELU AdamW,T256,bs16: 2LN beat1LN at Delta .0256/.0512/.0768 (CE .67619 vs .68153 at .0768). Base-lab same optimizer type/lr, mixed architectures: moreLN36/51 high (37sets,ratio.891),14/32 low (26sets,1.001); older opposite LN counts use an unidentified filter. Audit includes SGD/Adagrad; no optimizer-specific LN law follows. Depth:K1065; <8features deeper7/7. No sharp .05 switch; do not extrapolate smooth preference to SGD/Adagrad.
[K1019] SGD vs ADAPTIVE optimizers: family-calibrated Delta is a proxy,NOT a plain-vs-momentum SGD rule. Fit368pairs. MSE momentum.9 raw|g|~.03: Adam-equivalent lr/3,largerDelta correct59/71 vs54/71 at .01; wins11/19 when adaptiveDelta<=4x its .01-estimate. Classification131/146 and plainSGD MSE keep .01;do NOT infer a momentum bonus at equal lr/(1-m). Bigram |g|~.003:m.9 ~Adam lr/30,plain~lr/300;correct68/70 vs63/70 at .01. Momentum LM beats adaptive1/18,nominal parity1/4. PlainSGD wins3/141 when adaptiveDelta>15x larger. MLP calibration assumes>=1LN;zeroLN:K1038. Parity needs direct matched evidence(R838be7703a),NOT this multiplier.
[K1020] Two-spiral MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T: moreLN is a conditional preference; at equalLN deeper residual is NOT guaranteed(K1087's1/2-turn reversal). Same residual status:moreLN163/206,CE ratio.79-.92. Plain-moreLN vs residual-fewerLN,Delta.03-.5:depth gap<=1 plain58/66(.85);residual>=2deeper6/8(.71),a small confounded sample,NOT an equal-LN law. Below .03 residual14/24;above .5 residual5/6. ZeroLN residual vs plain>=1LN:below .5 residual8/59,above .5 10/13. High-rate RMSprop/2-3-turn smooth-candidate exception:K1077. Activation,width,data/budget matter;no LN+residual score or complete ranking follows.
[K1022] LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.
[K1033] Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).
[K1038] SGD vs adaptive,SGD calibrated Delta>=3x rival,rivalDelta<.1: deep(>=3) ZERO-LN smooth MLPs are task-dependent, not automatically frozen. Explicit plain-MSE/CE base-lab: deep SGD wins11/30 in11sets,loss ratio1.056; plain3/15(1.897),residual8/15(.991). Regression5/21; spiral4/5; XOR2/4: do NOT apply a universal penalty. Almost all use m=.9; budgets4096/8192samples; no deep rectifier cases. With >=1LN,SGD wins413/471(ratio.578). Older broader21/60 and493/563 use different filters. Keep residual,task,activation and budget scope; loss ratios do not measure parameter motion. Calibration:K1019.
[K1039] SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).
[K1040] Easy1-1.5-turn spiral CE,matched net/optimizer/lr/budget: coupled-Adam decay can matter at tiny losses; do not assume wd<=1e-4 is harmless. Older d2/w48/plainReLU,lr.003,T1024:Adamwd>=.001 loses to AdamW/wd0 (12/12 cells,CE ratio.002-.03). New fixed d2/w256/residualSiLU/2LN,Adam,T2048,bs16:wd1e-4 vs1e-5 raises CE8.21x atlr1e-4 (.00012268 vs .000014944),7.19x atlr.001 (.00012523 vs .000017412);one1.5-turn dataset,10seed means(R7dd7d943d3). These tiny absolute losses do not locate a decay threshold or rank different recipes. q_fb4a7f changes lr AND wd;no isolated cause. No transfer to harder spirals,RMSprop,Adagrad or LMs.

snaps.render:
[K1001] For shared-model/data/budget optimizer comparisons BELOW task-specific saturation, use cumulative displacement Δ as a progress proxy, not a universal test-loss ranking. Check K1004/K1071-K1073 before choosing maximum Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T; Adagrad: 2·lr·√T; SGD: lr·T·|g|/(1-m), |g|≈0.01 (bigram 0.003; momentum MSE 0.03, K1019). Older backtests favored larger Δ in ~85% after ceiling exceptions, but not every 256-2048-step task is under-trained. Across different architectures or optimizers, close Δ estimates are not decisive (K1012); use scoped architecture rules. Long-budget spiral/XOR maxima can lose (q_fb4a7f/q_46d72e); no validated general ceiling yet.
[K1002] Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW on the SAME architecture/budget: Adagrad Δ≈2·lr·√T, so comparable progress needs lr≈√T/2 (8-23×) higher. At lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3, Adam-family wins65/70; ratio10 is mixed4/7; ratio≥30 Adagrad wins9/9. For shared-architecture Adagrad rate comparisons, larger lr usually wins (original40/41; broader univariate lab73/78, history13/16), not always; lr3e-3 is not a universal safety guarantee. Do not use this rate preference to settle LN/activation changes (q_cd8a07). At lr≤1e-4, Δ≤0.01 over T≤2048 indicates little progress relative to adaptive rates≥3e-5, but freezing is approximate.
[K1003] SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.
[K1004] LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. snaps.label: kb_0004
snaps.render:
[K1001] For shared-model/data/budget optimizer comparisons BELOW task-specific saturation, use cumulative displacement Δ as a progress proxy, not a universal test-loss ranking. Check K1004/K1071-K1073 before choosing maximum Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T; Adagrad: 2·lr·√T; SGD: lr·T·|g|/(1-m), |g|≈0.01 (bigram 0.003; momentum MSE 0.03, K1019). Older backtests favored larger Δ in ~85% after ceiling exceptions, but not every 256-2048-step task is under-trained. Across different architectures or optimizers, close Δ estimates are not decisive (K1012); use scoped architecture rules. Long-budget spiral/XOR maxima can lose (q_fb4a7f/q_46d72e); no validated general ceiling yet.
[K1002] Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW on the SAME architecture/budget: Adagrad Δ≈2·lr·√T, so comparable progress needs lr≈√T/2 (8-23×) higher. At lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3, Adam-family wins65/70; ratio10 is mixed4/7; ratio≥30 Adagrad wins9/9. For shared-architecture Adagrad rate comparisons, larger lr usually wins (original40/41; broader univariate lab73/78, history13/16), not always; lr3e-3 is not a universal safety guarantee. Do not use this rate preference to settle LN/activation changes (q_cd8a07). At lr≤1e-4, Δ≤0.01 over T≤2048 indicates little progress relative to adaptive rates≥3e-5, but freezing is approximate.
[K1003] Normalized MLPs or bigram LMs,SGD vs adaptive BELOW saturation: plain SGD is often slow,NOT automatically frozen or last. It lost138/141 pairs when adaptiveDelta>15x its estimate(K1019); old all-family appearance wins~8% are pooled,not same-model controls. Momentum.9 lr.001-.003 is a contender,not guaranteed winner: general Adam-equivalent rate~lr/10,bigram~lr/30,MSE~lr/3. At lr<=.0003 it usually loses to same-lr adaptive below saturation. Calibration is a proxy,NOT proof momentum beats plain at equal lr/(1-m);q_0a12ba favors plain at parity,with decay differing. Deep zeroLN smooth MLPs need task-specific scope(K1038).
[K1004] LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. MSE RMSprop lr≥1e-3: versus ≥3× smaller Δ, wins22/36 corpus (better MLP6/6, equal12/22, worse4/8); at equal lr prefer Adam (RMSprop3e-3 loses33/35). Univariate lower-RMSprop-rate preference can occur even below this ceiling (K1063). Bigram optima depend on model width (K1071); wide multilayer univariate high-Δ fitting risk is comparative, not automatic last place (K1072). Tabular optimum changes with epochs/data rule (K1073). Short-budget XOR/spiral often benefit from high rates, but T2048 winners q_46d72e/q_fb4a7f refute blanket long-budget safety; no general replacement ceiling is validated.
[K1005] Shared-model optimizer comparisons BELOW saturation: minor decay/beta differences are weak tie-breakers,not universal noise; a clear undertraining gap usually matters more. Older same-arch higher-wd3/13,all loss gaps<1%;equal-lr Adam/AdamW5/10,beta2.95vs.9997/11. Do NOT assume those knobs are harmless in converged CE or long-budget recipes. Matched easy-spiral controls show coupled-Adam decay penalties atwd>=.001 AND wd1e-4(K1040);different lr/net recipes cannot be ranked from decay alone. q_a57013 at32epochs and q_38909f atT2048 change rate/betas/decay together;their gold does not isolate a 'minor knob' cause or justify blindly maximizing Delta.
[K1006] MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T,lowDelta: LN count is task-specific evidence,NOT LN+residual scoring or a deterministic rank. Older moreLN corpus:multivariate61/72,univariate57/69,tabular41/45;not factor-isolated. Multivariate plain+1LN vsres(K1076):mixed lab23/31,median MSE ratio.906;matched type/lr4/6,no full-config pairs;plain+1depth4/9(ratio1.166) opposes it. Equal-LN regression rectifier evidence(K1008) is not a forced tie-break across residual/tail differences. Regression depth:K1074;multivariate limit:K1080;SGD:K1039;spiral:K1020/K1066;plain tails:K1061(SGD strongest);XOR:K1018/K1065;tabular:K1009/K1033. No universal scoring formula.
[K1008] MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).
[K1009] Tabular CE,1024 rows,shared optimizer/lr/T,Delta>=.1: shallow and smooth are separate preferences; fewer-LN depends on data rule/budget. Old corpus: shallow21/26,smooth16/16; width not isolated. Base-lab moreLN wins: piecewise9/17 (17sets,CE ratio.987),smooth_additive5/13 (11sets,1.196),sparse_interaction0/10 (5sets,1.495). Same optimizer type/lr, but mixed architecture/decay; T256,4096/8192samples,NOT32epochs. Below .1 old moreLN41/45,deeper35/52; 32-epoch depth reversal can start near .03(K1033). Optimizer optima:K1073; activation:K1056. Do not discard residual+LN solely for smoothness or width(q_11a5f0); no universal additive score.
[K1012] For mixed choices, close cross-optimizer Δ estimates are uncertain; a 25% edge is not decisive (q_77d140). BELOW task/model saturation, ≥4× Δ favors progress over architecture (higher wins35/40 even against ≥2 extra LN/residual). Within ~3×, better architecture wins11/19: a weak preference, not a deterministic rank. Once both Δ≳0.3 extra Δ wins only≈62%; check K1004/K1063/K1071-K1073 and data/budget before sorting by Δ. Near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2/lnV, MSE≈Var(y)) are a tied bottom group; use architecture rather than tiny rate differences. No universal RMSprop-over-Adagrad correction is validated for near-parity LM comparisons.
[K1015] MLP residual/depth at shared optimizer/lr/T: residual status is NOT a task-wide trump card. Older confounded corpus: deeper plain regression beats shallower residual24/39; classification deeper residual beats shallow plain33/47,shallow residual beats deep plain19/32. These counts do not isolate skips or justify 'never choose deep plain'. Terminal LN,activation,features and budget matter:K1061,K1065,K1033,K1074. q_6e56f3 at32epochs favors3-block plain over5-block residual; q_611798/q_bca005 reverse identical recipes across1/2-turn datasets. Deep residual appearance53% vs plain29% is not a matched comparison or universal residual+depth rank.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).
[K1017] Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model, layer count: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 FEWER layers wins 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a); Δ≥0.5 fewer 8/11; 0.02≤Δ<0.1 COIN FLIP (fewer 8/15; q_4f69f2, q_9344eb: 2-layer beat 1-layer) - do not decide by depth there; Δ<0.02 deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE - wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 smaller wins 5/6, order by d_model ascending then layers (q_17f213; K1068). GRU vs transformer: K1075; lr: K1071.
[K1018] XOR CE,1024 rows,>=8 features,shared Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr/T,Delta>=.05: smooth is favored (older lab15/16, CE ratio.78; corpus6/6), but fewer LN is NOT validated. Fixed width24 depth2 plain GELU AdamW,T256,bs16: 2LN beat1LN at Delta .0256/.0512/.0768 (CE .67619 vs .68153 at .0768). Base-lab same optimizer type/lr, mixed architectures: moreLN36/51 high (37sets,ratio.891),14/32 low (26sets,1.001); older opposite LN counts use an unidentified filter. Audit includes SGD/Adagrad; no optimizer-specific LN law follows. Depth:K1065; <8features deeper7/7. No sharp .05 switch; do not extrapolate smooth preference to SGD/Adagrad.
[K1019] SGD vs ADAPTIVE optimizers: family-calibrated Delta is a proxy,NOT a plain-vs-momentum SGD rule. Fit368pairs. MSE momentum.9 raw|g|~.03: Adam-equivalent lr/3,largerDelta correct59/71 vs54/71 at .01; wins11/19 when adaptiveDelta<=4x its .01-estimate. Classification131/146 and plainSGD MSE keep .01;do NOT infer a momentum bonus at equal lr/(1-m). Bigram |g|~.003:m.9 ~Adam lr/30,plain~lr/300;correct68/70 vs63/70 at .01. Momentum LM beats adaptive1/18,nominal parity1/4. PlainSGD wins3/141 when adaptiveDelta>15x larger. MLP calibration assumes>=1LN;zeroLN:K1038. Parity needs direct matched evidence(R838be7703a),NOT this multiplier.
[K1020] Two-spiral MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T: moreLN is a conditional preference; at equalLN deeper residual is NOT guaranteed(K1097/K1099's1/2-turn reversal). Same residual status:moreLN163/206,CE ratio.79-.92. Plain-moreLN vs residual-fewerLN,Delta.03-.5:depth gap<=1 plain58/66(.85);residual>=2deeper6/8(.71),a small confounded sample,NOT an equal-LN law. Below .03 residual14/24;above .5 residual5/6. ZeroLN residual vs plain>=1LN:below .5 residual8/59,above .5 10/13. High-rate RMSprop/2-3-turn smooth-candidate exception:K1077. Activation,width,data/budget matter;no LN+residual score or complete ranking follows.
[K1022] Tabular CE or multivariate MSE ONLY,shared optimizer/lr/T,Delta<.1,equal LN count AND residual status: later LN is a weak tie-break,NOT a depth/activation override (lab4/7,loss ratio.99). Corpus11/12 pairs,median ratio.80;controlled smooth-additive2/2(.95);q_7ae5d3 agrees. Width/depth/activation remain confounded. q_30aef7's deeper residual GELU recipe beats shallow terminal-LN SiLU recipes,so placement cannot force their order. Not univariate MSE or XOR(corpus2/8;controlled univariate1/4),nor Delta>=.1(3/6). An advantage over one extra early LN remains untested.
[K1033] Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).
[K1038] SGD vs adaptive,SGD calibrated Delta>=3x rival,rivalDelta<.1: deep(>=3) ZERO-LN smooth MLPs are task-dependent, not automatically frozen. Explicit plain-MSE/CE base-lab: deep SGD wins11/30 in11sets,loss ratio1.056; plain3/15(1.897),residual8/15(.991). Regression5/21; spiral4/5; XOR2/4: do NOT apply a universal penalty. Almost all use m=.9; budgets4096/8192samples; no deep rectifier cases. With >=1LN,SGD wins413/471(ratio.578). Older broader21/60 and493/563 use different filters. Keep residual,task,activation and budget scope; loss ratios do not measure parameter motion. Calibration:K1019.
[K1039] SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).
[K1040] Easy1-1.5-turn spiral CE,matched net/optimizer/lr/budget: coupled-Adam decay can matter at tiny losses; do not assume wd<=1e-4 is harmless. Older d2/w48/plainReLU,lr.003,T1024:Adamwd>=.001 loses to AdamW/wd0 (12/12 cells,CE ratio.002-.03). New fixed d2/w256/residualSiLU/2LN,Adam,T2048,bs16:wd1e-4 vs1e-5 raises CE8.21x atlr1e-4 (.00012268 vs .000014944),7.19x atlr.001 (.00012523 vs .000017412);one1.5-turn dataset,10seed means(R7dd7d943d3). These tiny absolute losses do not locate a decay threshold or rank different recipes. q_fb4a7f changes lr AND wd;no isolated cause. No transfer to harder spirals,RMSprop,Adagrad or LMs.
[K1056] TABULAR classification (synthetic, 1024 rows), once trained (shared core-rule Δ≥0.1, same optimizer/lr/T): prefer GELU/SiLU over ReLU/LeakyReLU. Smooth wins 23/25 lab within-set pairs (~11 sets, median test-CE ratio ~0.80; smooth_additive 14/14, sparse_interaction 5/6, piecewise 4/5); corpus 16/16 (K1009). At Δ 0.01-0.1 only a tendency (44/74, ratio 0.87); at Δ<0.01 no effect (8/19, ratio 1.00) - decide by LN/depth instead. Activation-only matched pairs 19/28. q_b68ab2: plain SiLU RMSprop 1e-4×2048 (Δ0.2) beat residual LeakyReLU nets at larger Δ.
[K1057] UNIVARIATE regression, same MLP, Adam/AdamW vs RMSprop: Adam-family wins at almost any lr pairing - lab 78/88 same-arch within-set pairs (median MSE ratio ~0.06): equal lr 21/24; Adam at 3-33x LOWER lr 21/23; Adam at 3-10x+ higher lr 36/41. Adam lr<=RMSprop lr subset: non-oscillatory targets 15/15 (ratio0.02), sin/cos(2*pi*x) targets 27/32 (0.18). Corpus4/5 (only loss: Adam3e-5 vs RMSprop3e-3,100x gap). Do not credit RMSprop's early-step amplification (q_7f8fb0:AdamW3e-5 beat RMSprop3e-5 and1e-4). Wide-net lr*T>=1 overshoot risk(K1072) is comparative,not automatic. NOT multivariate(lab10/18,ratio.97;corpus5/9).
[K1059] Classification MLPs (tabular, XOR, spiral), NON-residual, depth≥2, all choices on the same SGD (plain or momentum): the net whose LAST hidden block has LayerNorm wins 31/31 lab within-set pairs (14 sets, median CE ratio 0.69) - even when it has FEWER LayerNorms in total (11/11, ratio 0.76). An unnormalized tail undoes earlier LN (q_1af0fa: a deep net with internal LN but 2 unnormalized final blocks lost to a shallower wider net; normalizing those blocks cut CE 0.69→0.47 in a controlled rerun). With adaptive optimizers the edge is weaker: Adam 70/102 (ratio 0.92), Adagrad 21/35 (~0.99). Regression: univariate 17/25, multivariate 20/35 - not reliable.

snaps.label: solve_e0004
snaps.render:
[K1001] For shared-model/data/budget optimizer comparisons BELOW task-specific saturation, use cumulative displacement Δ as a progress proxy, not a universal test-loss ranking. Check K1004/K1071-K1073 before choosing maximum Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T; Adagrad: 2·lr·√T; SGD: lr·T·|g|/(1-m), |g|≈0.01 (bigram 0.003; momentum MSE 0.03, K1019). Older backtests favored larger Δ in ~85% after ceiling exceptions, but not every 256-2048-step task is under-trained. Across different architectures or optimizers, close Δ estimates are not decisive (K1012); use scoped architecture rules. Long-budget spiral/XOR maxima can lose (q_fb4a7f/q_46d72e); no validated general ceiling yet.
[K1002] Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW on the SAME architecture/budget: Adagrad Δ≈2·lr·√T, so comparable progress needs lr≈√T/2 (8-23×) higher. At lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3, Adam-family wins65/70; ratio10 is mixed4/7; ratio≥30 Adagrad wins9/9. For shared-architecture Adagrad rate comparisons, larger lr usually wins (original40/41; broader univariate lab73/78, history13/16), not always; lr3e-3 is not a universal safety guarantee. Do not use this rate preference to settle LN/activation changes (q_cd8a07). At lr≤1e-4, Δ≤0.01 over T≤2048 indicates little progress relative to adaptive rates≥3e-5, but freezing is approximate.
[K1003] Normalized MLPs or bigram LMs,SGD vs adaptive BELOW saturation: plain SGD is often slow,NOT automatically frozen or last. It lost138/141 pairs when adaptiveDelta>15x its estimate(K1019); old all-family appearance wins~8% are pooled,not same-model controls. Momentum.9 lr.001-.003 is a contender,not guaranteed winner: general Adam-equivalent rate~lr/10,bigram~lr/30,MSE~lr/3. At lr<=.0003 it usually loses to same-lr adaptive below saturation. Calibration is a proxy,NOT proof momentum beats plain at equal lr/(1-m);q_0a12ba favors plain at parity,with decay differing. Deep zeroLN smooth MLPs need task-specific scope(K1038).
[K1004] LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. MSE RMSprop lr≥1e-3: versus ≥3× smaller Δ, wins22/36 corpus (better MLP6/6, equal12/22, worse4/8); at equal lr prefer Adam (RMSprop3e-3 loses33/35). Univariate lower-RMSprop-rate preference can occur even below this ceiling (K1063). Bigram optima depend on model width (K1071); wide multilayer univariate high-Δ fitting risk is comparative, not automatic last place (K1072). Tabular optimum changes with epochs/data rule (K1073). Short-budget XOR/spiral often benefit from high rates, but T2048 winners q_46d72e/q_fb4a7f refute blanket long-budget safety; no general replacement ceiling is validated.
[K1005] Shared-model optimizer comparisons BELOW saturation: minor decay/beta differences are weak tie-breakers,not universal noise; a clear undertraining gap usually matters more. Older same-arch higher-wd3/13,all loss gaps<1%;equal-lr Adam/AdamW5/10,beta2.95vs.9997/11. Do NOT assume those knobs are harmless in converged CE or long-budget recipes. Matched easy-spiral controls show coupled-Adam decay penalties atwd>=.001 AND wd1e-4(K1040);different lr/net recipes cannot be ranked from decay alone. q_a57013 at32epochs and q_38909f atT2048 change rate/betas/decay together;their gold does not isolate a 'minor knob' cause or justify blindly maximizing Delta.
[K1006] MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T,lowDelta: LN count is task-specific evidence,NOT LN+residual scoring or a deterministic rank. Older moreLN corpus:multivariate61/72,univariate57/69,tabular41/45;not factor-isolated. Multivariate plain+1LN vsres(K1076):mixed lab23/31,median MSE ratio.906;matched type/lr4/6,no full-config pairs;plain+1depth4/9(ratio1.166) opposes it. Equal-LN regression rectifier evidence(K1008) is not a forced tie-break across residual/tail differences. Regression depth:K1074;multivariate limit:K1080;SGD:K1039;spiral:K1020/K1066;plain tails:K1061(SGD strongest);XOR:K1018/K1065;tabular:K1009/K1033. No universal scoring formula.
[K1008] MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).
[K1009] Tabular CE,1024 rows,shared optimizer/lr/T,Delta>=.1: shallow and smooth are separate preferences; fewer-LN depends on data rule/budget. Old corpus: shallow21/26,smooth16/16; width not isolated. Base-lab moreLN wins: piecewise9/17 (17sets,CE ratio.987),smooth_additive5/13 (11sets,1.196),sparse_interaction0/10 (5sets,1.495). Same optimizer type/lr, but mixed architecture/decay; T256,4096/8192samples,NOT32epochs. Below .1 old moreLN41/45,deeper35/52; 32-epoch depth reversal can start near .03(K1033). Optimizer optima:K1073; activation:K1056. Do not discard residual+LN solely for smoothness or width(q_11a5f0); no universal additive score.
[K1012] For mixed choices, close cross-optimizer Δ estimates are uncertain; a 25% edge is not decisive (q_77d140). BELOW task/model saturation, ≥4× Δ favors progress over architecture (higher wins35/40 even against ≥2 extra LN/residual). Within ~3×, better architecture wins11/19: a weak preference, not a deterministic rank. Once both Δ≳0.3 extra Δ wins only≈62%; check K1004/K1063/K1071-K1073 and data/budget before sorting by Δ. Near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2/lnV, MSE≈Var(y)) are a tied bottom group; use architecture rather than tiny rate differences. No universal RMSprop-over-Adagrad correction is validated for near-parity LM comparisons.
[K1015] MLP residual/depth at shared optimizer/lr/T: residual status is NOT a task-wide trump card. Older confounded corpus: deeper plain regression beats shallower residual24/39; classification deeper residual beats shallow plain33/47,shallow residual beats deep plain19/32. These counts do not isolate skips or justify 'never choose deep plain'. Terminal LN,activation,features and budget matter:K1061,K1065,K1033,K1074. q_6e56f3 at32epochs favors3-block plain over5-block residual; q_611798/q_bca005 reverse identical recipes across1/2-turn datasets. Deep residual appearance53% vs plain29% is not a matched comparison or universal residual+depth rank.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).
[K1017] Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model, layer count: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 FEWER layers wins 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a); Δ≥0.5 fewer 8/11; 0.02≤Δ<0.1 COIN FLIP (fewer 8/15; q_4f69f2, q_9344eb: 2-layer beat 1-layer) - do not decide by depth there; Δ<0.02 deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE - wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 smaller wins 5/6, order by d_model ascending then layers (q_17f213; K1068). GRU vs transformer: K1075; lr: K1071.
[K1018] XOR CE,1024 rows,>=8 features,shared Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr/T,Delta>=.05: smooth is favored (older lab15/16, CE ratio.78; corpus6/6), but fewer LN is NOT validated. Fixed width24 depth2 plain GELU AdamW,T256,bs16: 2LN beat1LN at Delta .0256/.0512/.0768 (CE .67619 vs .68153 at .0768). Base-lab same optimizer type/lr, mixed architectures: moreLN36/51 high (37sets,ratio.891),14/32 low (26sets,1.001); older opposite LN counts use an unidentified filter. Audit includes SGD/Adagrad; no optimizer-specific LN law follows. Depth:K1065; <8features deeper7/7. No sharp .05 switch; do not extrapolate smooth preference to SGD/Adagrad.
[K1019] SGD vs ADAPTIVE optimizers: family-calibrated Delta is a proxy,NOT a plain-vs-momentum SGD rule. Fit368pairs. MSE momentum.9 raw|g|~.03: Adam-equivalent lr/3,largerDelta correct59/71 vs54/71 at .01; wins11/19 when adaptiveDelta<=4x its .01-estimate. Classification131/146 and plainSGD MSE keep .01;do NOT infer a momentum bonus at equal lr/(1-m). Bigram |g|~.003:m.9 ~Adam lr/30,plain~lr/300;correct68/70 vs63/70 at .01. Momentum LM beats adaptive1/18,nominal parity1/4. PlainSGD wins3/141 when adaptiveDelta>15x larger. MLP calibration assumes>=1LN;zeroLN:K1038. Parity needs direct matched evidence(R838be7703a),NOT this multiplier.
[K1020] Two-spiral MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T: moreLN is a conditional preference; at equalLN deeper residual is NOT guaranteed(K1087's1/2-turn reversal). Same residual status:moreLN163/206,CE ratio.79-.92. Plain-moreLN vs residual-fewerLN,Delta.03-.5:depth gap<=1 plain58/66(.85);residual>=2deeper6/8(.71),a small confounded sample,NOT an equal-LN law. Below .03 residual14/24;above .5 residual5/6. ZeroLN residual vs plain>=1LN:below .5 residual8/59,above .5 10/13. High-rate RMSprop/2-3-turn smooth-candidate exception:K1077. Activation,width,data/budget matter;no LN+residual score or complete ranking follows.
[K1022] LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.
[K1033] Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).
[K1038] SGD vs adaptive,SGD calibrated Delta>=3x rival,rivalDelta<.1: deep(>=3) ZERO-LN smooth MLPs are task-dependent, not automatically frozen. Explicit plain-MSE/CE base-lab: deep SGD wins11/30 in11sets,loss ratio1.056; plain3/15(1.897),residual8/15(.991). Regression5/21; spiral4/5; XOR2/4: do NOT apply a universal penalty. Almost all use m=.9; budgets4096/8192samples; no deep rectifier cases. With >=1LN,SGD wins413/471(ratio.578). Older broader21/60 and493/563 use different filters. Keep residual,task,activation and budget scope; loss ratios do not measure parameter motion. Calibration:K1019.
[K1039] SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).
[K1040] Easy1-1.5-turn spiral CE,matched net/optimizer/lr/budget: coupled-Adam decay can matter at tiny losses; do not assume wd<=1e-4 is harmless. Older d2/w48/plainReLU,lr.003,T1024:Adamwd>=.001 loses to AdamW/wd0 (12/12 cells,CE ratio.002-.03). New fixed d2/w256/residualSiLU/2LN,Adam,T2048,bs16:wd1e-4 vs1e-5 raises CE8.21x atlr1e-4 (.00012268 vs .000014944),7.19x atlr.001 (.00012523 vs .000017412);one1.5-turn dataset,10seed means(R7dd7d943d3). These tiny absolute losses do not locate a decay threshold or rank different recipes. q_fb4a7f changes lr AND wd;no isolated cause. No transfer to harder spirals,RMSprop,Adagrad or LMs.
[K1056] TABULAR classification (synthetic, 1024 rows), once trained (shared core-rule Δ≥0.1, same optimizer/lr/T): prefer GELU/SiLU over ReLU/LeakyReLU. Smooth wins 23/25 lab within-set pairs (~11 sets, median test-CE ratio ~0.80; smooth_additive 14/14, sparse_interaction 5/6, piecewise 4/5); corpus 16/16 (K1009). At Δ 0.01-0.1 only a tendency (44/74, ratio 0.87); at Δ<0.01 no effect (8/19, ratio 1.00) - decide by LN/depth instead. Activation-only matched pairs 19/28. q_b68ab2: plain SiLU RMSprop 1e-4×2048 (Δ0.2) beat residual LeakyReLU nets at larger Δ.
[K1057] UNIVARIATE regression, same MLP, Adam/AdamW vs RMSprop: Adam-family wins at almost any lr pairing - lab 78/88 same-arch within-set pairs (median MSE ratio ~0.06): equal lr 21/24; Adam at 3-33× LOWER lr 21/23; Adam at 3-10×+ higher lr 36/41. Adam lr≤RMSprop lr subset: non-oscillatory targets 15/15 (ratio 0.02), sin/cos(2πx) targets 27/32 (0.18). Corpus 4/5 (only loss: Adam 3e-5 vs RMSprop 3e-3, 100× gap). Do not credit RMSprop's early-step amplification (q_7f8fb0: AdamW 3e-5 beat RMSprop 3e-5 and 1e-4). Wide-net lr·T≥1 overshoot (K1055) still applies first. NOT multivariate (lab 10/18, ratio 0.97; corpus 5/9).
[K1059] Classification MLPs (tabular, XOR, spiral), NON-residual, depth≥2, all choices on the same SGD (plain or momentum): the net whose LAST hidden block has LayerNorm wins 31/31 lab within-set pairs (14 sets, median CE ratio 0.69) - even when it has FEWER LayerNorms in total (11/11, ratio 0.76). An unnormalized tail undoes earlier LN (q_1af0fa: a deep net with internal LN but 2 unnormalized final blocks lost to a shallower wider net; normalizing those blocks cut CE 0.69→0.47 in a controlled rerun). With adaptive optimizers the edge is weaker: Adam 70/102 (ratio 0.92), Adagrad 21/35 (~0.99). Regression: univariate 17/25, multivariate 20/35 - not reliable.
[K1061] Classification MLPs,shared SGD/lr/T,Delta<.1: residual beats depth>=4 plain with MORE LN and an unnormalized last block (lab16/16,CE ratio.72). NOT an adaptive ranking rule (lab5/9); extra plain LNs still count. Old corpus residual5/5 is recipe-confounded. Plain last-block LN: XOR+SGD plain9/10; spiral+Adam-family plain22/23 (residual/plain CE1.3-1.4); spiral+SGD residual3/3 plus controlled2/2 (ratio.3-.8); tabular plain12/27 lab,6/6 corpus. Moving plain LN to last block lowered CE6/6 controlled cells,not a universal tail penalty. Equal-LN rivals and Delta>=.1 are outside scope. q_fba153/q_99babc expose adaptive overuse.
[K1063] UNIVARIATE regression, RMSprop vs RMSprop (same MLP, different lr): the LOWER RMSprop lr usually wins, even at small Δ — lab larger-lr wins 9/42 (10 experiment groups; T=256 width≥128: 3/24, median MSE ratio 3.6; lr 1e-4 vs 3e-5: 3/11), corpus 2/3. At T=1024 on narrow nets it is a coin flip (4/9). RMSprop as the larger-Δ choice against Adam/AdamW of the same net also loses (lab 0/21 at RMSprop lr≥3e-4). Do not apply max-Δ to RMSprop on univariate MSE; multivariate is a coin flip (11/25).
[K1065] XOR with ≥8 input features, once trained (shared optimizer, Δ≥0.05): depth helps only WITH residuals. A deeper NON-residual MLP loses to a shallower one even at a 1-2 block gap (lab deeper wins 1/31, 13 sets, CE ×1.23); a deeper RESIDUAL MLP beats a shallower one at a 1-2 block gap (8/13, 7 sets, CE ×0.82) but loses at gap ≥3 (lab 0/4, corpus 2-vs-5 block 2/3 shallow, K1018). q_164857 (AdamW 1e-4×2048): 3-block residual SiLU nets beat 1-block w192 nets, and the 3-block non-residual GELU net was last. At Δ<0.05 depth is a coin flip (plain 10/25, residual 14/19 deeper wins).
[K1066] TWO-SPIRAL classification, DEEP vs SHALLOW (same optimizer): a deeper (≥3 block) RESIDUAL MLP with MORE LayerNorms than a shallow (≤2 block) net wins almost always — lab 51/55 (adaptive Δ≥0.05 34/35, CE ratio 0.38; adaptive Δ<0.05 11/14; SGD 6/6, ratio 0.36), corpus 8/8 (ratio 0.76) — even if the shallow net is much wider. Deeper NON-residual nets are unreliable: lab 30/32 with more LN but corpus 0/7 (q_5fe255, q_774f6c had unnormalized last blocks) — credit them only if their last block is LN'd (K1061). Deeper residual with ≤ the shallow net's LN: lab 33/43, corpus 0/2 — tendency only. q_d7ea11: 3-LN residual deep net beat the shallow wide pick.
[K1068] BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER d_model × Δ (same optimizer/lr/T, different d_model): wider wins only while under-trained; the flip is at Δ≈0.1. Δ 0.02-0.1: LARGER d_model wins (lab 21/23, corpus 13/13, CE ratio ~0.98). Δ 0.1-0.5 (e.g. Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024): SMALLER d_model wins (lab 26/27 — d64 beat d128 20/21, d32 beat d128 2/2 with ratio 1.14; corpus 7/11, d64 vs d128 3/3). Δ≥0.5: smaller wins (lab 10/12, corpus 5/6). Δ<0.02: coin flip, SGD favors wider. Fills K1017's gap. q_02539d: d128 AdamW 3e-4×512 (Δ0.15) lost to d64 RMSprop 3e-3×512.
[K1069] BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER head count (same d_model/layers/optimizer/T): fewer heads (2 vs 4) wins 12/15 lab pairs. At Δ<0.5 it is only a tie-break (CE ratio ≈1.00); at Δ≥0.5 it matters (lab 4/4, ratio 1.01-1.07; controlled q_d6dddb d128 AdamW 3e-3×256: 2 heads −0.18 nats vs 4 heads, d_ff 128→256 only +0.07) and head count outranks a 2× d_ff difference (fewer heads + larger d_ff beat more heads + smaller d_ff 4/4). q_d6dddb gold: 2-head d_ff256 beat 4-head d_ff128. Order: d_model/layers (K1017) first, then heads, then d_ff.
[K1070] Classification MLPs,SAME net/lr,T<=1024: RMSprop is an underfitting-regime preference,NOT a guaranteed winner on easy high-rate spirals(K1086). Older matched17/20,median Adam/RMS CE1.12;controlled7/8. Do not use a universal1.5x lr conversion. Edge shrank with T;T2048 Adam1/1. Exact d4w24 residual LeakyReLU recipes atlr.003,T256 favor Adam on1turn(q_7e1811),RMSprop on2turns(q_95fe03);wd/betas and dataset confound cause. Atlr<=3e-4 older RMS wins multivariate4/4,bigram4/4;atlr>=.001 Adam wins multivariate6/6,bigram transformer5/5. Univariate:K1057. Close cross-optimizer Delta is not a total order;later fit/recipe/data matter.
[K1071] Bigram LM,SAME model/data: for d128 post-LN transformers do NOT dismiss Delta<.03 rivals as frozen (q_ef498d;Raeabecdef0). Old d128 Delta.03-.1 rivals beat largerDelta11/11. For d32/d64 TF/GRU,old favorable band.1-.3: >=2x more loses TF43/44,GRU5/6 (CE+2-20%); Delta>=1 loses to rival>=.03 in17/17. Below old band,higher wins TF13/13,GRU14/15;this is NOT a d128/conservative-rival law. Old nearest-.2(.1 for d128) heuristic52/65 vs max43/65 is recipe-confounded,not optimum proof. Width,optimizer/lr,budget,loss and initialization remain conditions; no universal sweet spot or overshoot mechanism.
[K1072] Univariate MSE,SAME depth>=2 width>=64 MLP: Delta>=1 is a relative overshoot RISK,not an automatic loss to Delta .1-.5. Older high-Delta wins:w64 0/12(MSE x8.8),w128 5/18(x5.5),w256 1/13(x4.4);controlled moderate wins11/12. Counterexample K1083:fixed zeroLN w128/d2 LeakyReLU Adam,T2048,highDelta6.144 MSE.01578 beats Delta.2048 MSE.35314. q_af3ba4 also favors highDelta above most slower recipes. No universal zeroLN exception or near-frozen rival cutoff. Width<=32,depth1 and multivariate are outside this ceiling's scope,NOT evidence of high-rate safety (multivariate reversal K1081). snaps.render:
[K1001] Optimizer comparison,SAME model/data/budget: use Delta as a progress proxy ONLY below task/model saturation. T256 can be32epochs; neither step count nor nominal parity proves adaptive or max-Delta wins. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop:lr*T;Adagrad:2*lr*sqrt(T);SGD:lr*T*|g|/(1-m),g~.01 (bigram.003,momentumMSE.03,K1019). Check K1004/K1071-K1073 and target/batch first;close mixed-recipe estimates:K1012. Old largerDelta~85% backtests were ceiling-filtered,not a law. Byte-identical q_561d81/q_21a335 recipes reverse winners on different targets/splits. Long XOR optimizer reversal K1119 is NOT a low-rate rule;no universal ceiling.
[K1002] Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW on the SAME architecture/budget: Adagrad Δ≈2·lr·√T, so comparable progress needs lr≈√T/2 (8-23×) higher. At lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3, Adam-family wins65/70; ratio10 is mixed4/7; ratio≥30 Adagrad wins9/9. For shared-architecture Adagrad rate comparisons, larger lr usually wins (original40/41; broader univariate lab73/78, history13/16), not always; lr3e-3 is not a universal safety guarantee. Do not use this rate preference to settle LN/activation changes (q_cd8a07). At lr≤1e-4, Δ≤0.01 over T≤2048 indicates little progress relative to adaptive rates≥3e-5, but freezing is approximate.
[K1003] Normalized MLPs or bigram LMs,SGD vs adaptive BELOW saturation: plain SGD is often slow,NOT automatically frozen or last. It lost138/141 pairs when adaptiveDelta>15x its estimate(K1019); old all-family appearance wins~8% are pooled,not same-model controls. Momentum.9 lr.001-.003 is a contender,not guaranteed winner: general Adam-equivalent rate~lr/10,bigram~lr/30,MSE~lr/3. At lr<=.0003 it usually loses to same-lr adaptive below saturation. Calibration is a proxy,NOT proof momentum beats plain at equal lr/(1-m);q_0a12ba favors plain at parity,with decay differing. Deep zeroLN smooth MLPs need task-specific scope(K1038).
[K1004] LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. MSE RMSprop lr≥1e-3: versus ≥3× smaller Δ, wins22/36 corpus (better MLP6/6, equal12/22, worse4/8); at equal lr prefer Adam (RMSprop3e-3 loses33/35). Univariate lower-RMSprop-rate preference can occur even below this ceiling (K1063). Bigram optima depend on model width (K1071); wide multilayer univariate high-Δ fitting risk is comparative, not automatic last place (K1072). Tabular optimum changes with epochs/data rule (K1073). Short-budget XOR/spiral often benefit from high rates, but T2048 winners q_46d72e/q_fb4a7f refute blanket long-budget safety; no general replacement ceiling is validated.
[K1005] Shared-model optimizer comparisons BELOW saturation: minor decay/beta differences are weak tie-breakers,not universal noise; a clear undertraining gap usually matters more. Older same-arch higher-wd3/13,all loss gaps<1%;equal-lr Adam/AdamW5/10,beta2.95vs.9997/11. Do NOT assume those knobs are harmless in converged CE or long-budget recipes. Matched easy-spiral controls show coupled-Adam decay penalties atwd>=.001 AND wd1e-4(K1040);different lr/net recipes cannot be ranked from decay alone. q_a57013 at32epochs and q_38909f atT2048 change rate/betas/decay together;their gold does not isolate a 'minor knob' cause or justify blindly maximizing Delta.
[K1006] MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T,lowDelta: LN count is task-specific evidence,NOT LN+residual scoring or a deterministic rank. Older moreLN corpus:multivariate61/72,univariate57/69,tabular41/45;not factor-isolated. Multivariate plain+1LN vsres(K1076):mixed lab23/31,median MSE ratio.906;matched type/lr4/6,no full-config pairs;plain+1depth4/9(ratio1.166) opposes it. Equal-LN regression rectifier evidence(K1008) is not a forced tie-break across residual/tail differences. Regression depth:K1074;multivariate limit:K1080;SGD:K1039;spiral:K1020/K1066;plain tails:K1061(SGD strongest);XOR:K1018/K1065;tabular:K1009/K1033. No universal scoring formula.

snaps.render:
[K1001] For shared-model/data/budget optimizer comparisons BELOW task-specific saturation, use cumulative displacement Δ as a progress proxy, not a universal test-loss ranking. Check K1004/K1071-K1073 before choosing maximum Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T; Adagrad: 2·lr·√T; SGD: lr·T·|g|/(1-m), |g|≈0.01 (bigram 0.003; momentum MSE 0.03, K1019). Older backtests favored larger Δ in ~85% after ceiling exceptions, but not every 256-2048-step task is under-trained. Across different architectures or optimizers, close Δ estimates are not decisive (K1012); use scoped architecture rules. Long-budget spiral/XOR maxima can lose (q_fb4a7f/q_46d72e); no validated general ceiling yet.
[K1002] Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW on the SAME architecture/budget: Adagrad Δ≈2·lr·√T, so comparable progress needs lr≈√T/2 (8-23×) higher. At lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3, Adam-family wins65/70; ratio10 is mixed4/7; ratio≥30 Adagrad wins9/9. For shared-architecture Adagrad rate comparisons, larger lr usually wins (original40/41; broader univariate lab73/78, history13/16), not always; lr3e-3 is not a universal safety guarantee. Do not use this rate preference to settle LN/activation changes (q_cd8a07). At lr≤1e-4, Δ≤0.01 over T≤2048 indicates little progress relative to adaptive rates≥3e-5, but freezing is approximate.
[K1003] Normalized MLPs or bigram LMs,SGD vs adaptive BELOW saturation: plain SGD is often slow,NOT automatically frozen or last. It lost138/141 pairs when adaptiveDelta>15x its estimate(K1019); old all-family appearance wins~8% are pooled,not same-model controls. Momentum.9 lr.001-.003 is a contender,not guaranteed winner: general Adam-equivalent rate~lr/10,bigram~lr/30,MSE~lr/3. At lr<=.0003 it usually loses to same-lr adaptive below saturation. Calibration is a proxy,NOT proof momentum beats plain at equal lr/(1-m);q_0a12ba favors plain at parity,with decay differing. Deep zeroLN smooth MLPs need task-specific scope(K1038).
[K1004] LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. MSE RMSprop lr≥1e-3: versus ≥3× smaller Δ, wins22/36 corpus (better MLP6/6, equal12/22, worse4/8); at equal lr prefer Adam (RMSprop3e-3 loses33/35). Univariate lower-RMSprop-rate preference can occur even below this ceiling (K1063). Bigram optima depend on model width (K1071); wide multilayer univariate high-Δ fitting risk is comparative, not automatic last place (K1072). Tabular optimum changes with epochs/data rule (K1073). Short-budget XOR/spiral often benefit from high rates, but T2048 winners q_46d72e/q_fb4a7f refute blanket long-budget safety; no general replacement ceiling is validated.
[K1005] Shared-model optimizer comparisons BELOW saturation: minor decay/beta differences are weak tie-breakers,not universal noise; a clear undertraining gap usually matters more. Older same-arch higher-wd3/13,all loss gaps<1%;equal-lr Adam/AdamW5/10,beta2.95vs.9997/11. Do NOT assume those knobs are harmless in converged CE or long-budget recipes. Matched easy-spiral controls show coupled-Adam decay penalties atwd>=.001 AND wd1e-4(K1040);different lr/net recipes cannot be ranked from decay alone. q_a57013 at32epochs and q_38909f atT2048 change rate/betas/decay together;their gold does not isolate a 'minor knob' cause or justify blindly maximizing Delta.
[K1006] MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T,lowDelta: LN count is task-specific evidence,NOT LN+residual scoring or a deterministic rank. Older moreLN corpus:multivariate61/72,univariate57/69,tabular41/45;not factor-isolated. Multivariate plain+1LN vsres(K1076):mixed lab23/31,median MSE ratio.906;matched type/lr4/6,no full-config pairs;plain+1depth4/9(ratio1.166) opposes it. Equal-LN regression rectifier evidence(K1008) is not a forced tie-break across residual/tail differences. Regression depth:K1074;multivariate limit:K1080;SGD:K1039;spiral:K1020/K1066;plain tails:K1061(SGD strongest);XOR:K1018/K1065;tabular:K1009/K1033. No universal scoring formula.
[K1008] MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).
[K1009] Tabular CE,1024 rows,shared optimizer/lr/T,Delta>=.1: shallow and smooth are separate preferences; fewer-LN depends on data rule/budget. Old corpus: shallow21/26,smooth16/16; width not isolated. Base-lab moreLN wins: piecewise9/17 (17sets,CE ratio.987),smooth_additive5/13 (11sets,1.196),sparse_interaction0/10 (5sets,1.495). Same optimizer type/lr, but mixed architecture/decay; T256,4096/8192samples,NOT32epochs. Below .1 old moreLN41/45,deeper35/52; 32-epoch depth reversal can start near .03(K1033). Optimizer optima:K1073; activation:K1056. Do not discard residual+LN solely for smoothness or width(q_11a5f0); no universal additive score.
[K1012] For mixed choices, close cross-optimizer Δ estimates are uncertain; a 25% edge is not decisive (q_77d140). BELOW task/model saturation, ≥4× Δ favors progress over architecture (higher wins35/40 even against ≥2 extra LN/residual). Within ~3×, better architecture wins11/19: a weak preference, not a deterministic rank. Once both Δ≳0.3 extra Δ wins only≈62%; check K1004/K1063/K1071-K1073 and data/budget before sorting by Δ. Near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2/lnV, MSE≈Var(y)) are a tied bottom group; use architecture rather than tiny rate differences. No universal RMSprop-over-Adagrad correction is validated for near-parity LM comparisons.
[K1015] MLP residual/depth at shared optimizer/lr/T: residual status is NOT a task-wide trump card. Older confounded corpus: deeper plain regression beats shallower residual24/39; classification deeper residual beats shallow plain33/47,shallow residual beats deep plain19/32. These counts do not isolate skips or justify 'never choose deep plain'. Terminal LN,activation,features and budget matter:K1061,K1065,K1033,K1074. q_6e56f3 at32epochs favors3-block plain over5-block residual; q_611798/q_bca005 reverse identical recipes across1/2-turn datasets. Deep residual appearance53% vs plain29% is not a matched comparison or universal residual+depth rank.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).
[K1017] Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model, layer count: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 FEWER layers wins 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a); Δ≥0.5 fewer 8/11; 0.02≤Δ<0.1 COIN FLIP (fewer 8/15; q_4f69f2, q_9344eb: 2-layer beat 1-layer) - do not decide by depth there; Δ<0.02 deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE - wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 smaller wins 5/6, order by d_model ascending then layers (q_17f213; K1068). GRU vs transformer: K1075; lr: K1071.
[K1018] XOR CE,1024 rows,>=8 features,shared Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr/T,Delta>=.05: smooth is favored (older lab15/16, CE ratio.78; corpus6/6), but fewer LN is NOT validated. Fixed width24 depth2 plain GELU AdamW,T256,bs16: 2LN beat1LN at Delta .0256/.0512/.0768 (CE .67619 vs .68153 at .0768). Base-lab same optimizer type/lr, mixed architectures: moreLN36/51 high (37sets,ratio.891),14/32 low (26sets,1.001); older opposite LN counts use an unidentified filter. Audit includes SGD/Adagrad; no optimizer-specific LN law follows. Depth:K1065; <8features deeper7/7. No sharp .05 switch; do not extrapolate smooth preference to SGD/Adagrad.
[K1019] SGD vs ADAPTIVE optimizers: family-calibrated Delta is a proxy,NOT a plain-vs-momentum SGD rule. Fit368pairs. MSE momentum.9 raw|g|~.03: Adam-equivalent lr/3,largerDelta correct59/71 vs54/71 at .01; wins11/19 when adaptiveDelta<=4x its .01-estimate. Classification131/146 and plainSGD MSE keep .01;do NOT infer a momentum bonus at equal lr/(1-m). Bigram |g|~.003:m.9 ~Adam lr/30,plain~lr/300;correct68/70 vs63/70 at .01. Momentum LM beats adaptive1/18,nominal parity1/4. PlainSGD wins3/141 when adaptiveDelta>15x larger. MLP calibration assumes>=1LN;zeroLN:K1038. Parity needs direct matched evidence(R838be7703a),NOT this multiplier.
[K1020] Two-spiral MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T: moreLN is a conditional preference; at equalLN deeper residual is NOT guaranteed(K1097/K1099's1/2-turn reversal). Same residual status:moreLN163/206,CE ratio.79-.92. Plain-moreLN vs residual-fewerLN,Delta.03-.5:depth gap<=1 plain58/66(.85);residual>=2deeper6/8(.71),a small confounded sample,NOT an equal-LN law. Below .03 residual14/24;above .5 residual5/6. ZeroLN residual vs plain>=1LN:below .5 residual8/59,above .5 10/13. High-rate RMSprop/2-3-turn smooth-candidate exception:K1077. Activation,width,data/budget matter;no LN+residual score or complete ranking follows.
[K1022] Tabular CE or multivariate MSE ONLY,shared optimizer/lr/T,Delta<.1,equal LN count AND residual status: later LN is a weak tie-break,NOT a depth/activation override (lab4/7,loss ratio.99). Corpus11/12 pairs,median ratio.80;controlled smooth-additive2/2(.95);q_7ae5d3 agrees. Width/depth/activation remain confounded. q_30aef7's deeper residual GELU recipe beats shallow terminal-LN SiLU recipes,so placement cannot force their order. Not univariate MSE or XOR(corpus2/8;controlled univariate1/4),nor Delta>=.1(3/6). An advantage over one extra early LN remains untested.
[K1033] Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).
[K1038] SGD vs adaptive,SGD calibrated Delta>=3x rival,rivalDelta<.1: deep(>=3) ZERO-LN smooth MLPs are task-dependent, not automatically frozen. Explicit plain-MSE/CE base-lab: deep SGD wins11/30 in11sets,loss ratio1.056; plain3/15(1.897),residual8/15(.991). Regression5/21; spiral4/5; XOR2/4: do NOT apply a universal penalty. Almost all use m=.9; budgets4096/8192samples; no deep rectifier cases. With >=1LN,SGD wins413/471(ratio.578). Older broader21/60 and493/563 use different filters. [K1001] Optimizer comparison,SAME model/data/budget: use Delta as a progress proxy ONLY below task/model saturation. T256 can be32epochs; neither step count nor nominal parity proves adaptive or max-Delta wins. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop:lr*T;Adagrad:2*lr*sqrt(T);SGD:lr*T*|g|/(1-m),g~.01 (bigram.003,momentumMSE.03,K1019). Check K1004/K1071-K1073 and target/batch first;close mixed-recipe estimates:K1012. Old largerDelta~85% backtests were ceiling-filtered,not a law. Byte-identical q_561d81/q_21a335 recipes reverse winners on different targets/splits. Long XOR optimizer reversal K1119 is NOT a low-rate rule;no universal ceiling.
[K1002] Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW on the SAME architecture/budget: Adagrad Δ≈2·lr·√T, so comparable progress needs lr≈√T/2 (8-23×) higher. At lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3, Adam-family wins65/70; ratio10 is mixed4/7; ratio≥30 Adagrad wins9/9. For shared-architecture Adagrad rate comparisons, larger lr usually wins (original40/41; broader univariate lab73/78, history13/16), not always; lr3e-3 is not a universal safety guarantee. Do not use this rate preference to settle LN/activation changes (q_cd8a07). At lr≤1e-4, Δ≤0.01 over T≤2048 indicates little progress relative to adaptive rates≥3e-5, but freezing is approximate.
[K1003] Normalized MLPs or bigram LMs,SGD vs adaptive BELOW saturation: plain SGD is often slow,NOT automatically frozen or last. It lost138/141 pairs when adaptiveDelta>15x its estimate(K1019); old all-family appearance wins~8% are pooled,not same-model controls. Momentum.9 lr.001-.003 is a contender,not guaranteed winner: general Adam-equivalent rate~lr/10,bigram~lr/30,MSE~lr/3. At lr<=.0003 it usually loses to same-lr adaptive below saturation. Calibration is a proxy,NOT proof momentum beats plain at equal lr/(1-m);q_0a12ba favors plain at parity,with decay differing. Deep zeroLN smooth MLPs need task-specific scope(K1038).
[K1004] LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. MSE RMSprop lr≥1e-3: versus ≥3× smaller Δ, wins22/36 corpus (better MLP6/6, equal12/22, worse4/8); at equal lr prefer Adam (RMSprop3e-3 loses33/35). Univariate lower-RMSprop-rate preference can occur even below this ceiling (K1063). Bigram optima depend on model width (K1071); wide multilayer univariate high-Δ fitting risk is comparative, not automatic last place (K1072). Tabular optimum changes with epochs/data rule (K1073). Short-budget XOR/spiral often benefit from high rates, but T2048 winners q_46d72e/q_fb4a7f refute blanket long-budget safety; no general replacement ceiling is validated.
[K1005] Shared-model optimizer comparisons BELOW saturation: minor decay/beta differences are weak tie-breakers,not universal noise; a clear undertraining gap usually matters more. Older same-arch higher-wd3/13,all loss gaps<1%;equal-lr Adam/AdamW5/10,beta2.95vs.9997/11. Do NOT assume those knobs are harmless in converged CE or long-budget recipes. Matched easy-spiral controls show coupled-Adam decay penalties atwd>=.001 AND wd1e-4(K1040);different lr/net recipes cannot be ranked from decay alone. q_a57013 at32epochs and q_38909f atT2048 change rate/betas/decay together;their gold does not isolate a 'minor knob' cause or justify blindly maximizing Delta.
[K1006] MLPs,shared optimizer/lr/T,lowDelta: LN count is task-specific evidence,NOT LN+residual scoring or a deterministic rank. Older moreLN corpus:multivariate61/72,univariate57/69,tabular41/45;not factor-isolated. Multivariate plain+1LN vsres(K1076):mixed lab23/31,median MSE ratio.906;matched type/lr4/6,no full-config pairs;plain+1depth4/9(ratio1.166) opposes it. Equal-LN regression rectifier evidence(K1008) is not a forced tie-break across residual/tail differences. Regression depth:K1074;multivariate limit:K1080;SGD:K1039;spiral:K1020/K1066;plain tails:K1061(SGD strongest);XOR:K1018/K1065;tabular:K1009/K1033. No universal scoring formula.
[K1008] MSE regression,SHARED optimizer/lr/T and EQUAL LN count: prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU to SiLU/GELU as a tendency,not a tie-break across residual/tail/rate changes. Smooth targets do not imply smooth activation. Older equal-LN multivariate37/52:SGD13/15(~2x MSE),adaptive24/37(~1.1x);activation-only univariate adaptive with>=2LN9/9(~14x),LeakyReLU>SiLU7/7. Fewer-LN rectifier17/33 is mixed,NOT mandatory LN-first(q_52be5a). Shared-SGD one-LN-gap:K1039. This activation evidence cannot reject faster momentumSGD SiLU for slower Adam rectifier(q_4c7053),or rank cross-optimizer choices(q_bdfcc1).
[K1009] Tabular CE,1024 rows,shared optimizer/lr/T,Delta>=.1: shallow and smooth are separate preferences; fewer-LN depends on data rule/budget. Old corpus: shallow21/26,smooth16/16; width not isolated. Base-lab moreLN wins: piecewise9/17 (17sets,CE ratio.987),smooth_additive5/13 (11sets,1.196),sparse_interaction0/10 (5sets,1.495). Same optimizer type/lr, but mixed architecture/decay; T256,4096/8192samples,NOT32epochs. Below .1 old moreLN41/45,deeper35/52; 32-epoch depth reversal can start near .03(K1033). Optimizer optima:K1073; activation:K1056. Do not discard residual+LN solely for smoothness or width(q_11a5f0); no universal additive score.
[K1012] Mixed-optimizer/architecture rankings: close Delta estimates are NOT winner evidence; even a25% edge is inconclusive. Below task/model saturation,old >=4x gap favors progress35/40;within3x architecture wins11/19,only a weak preference. Once both Delta>=.3,extra wins~62%;check task/model/budget(K1004/K1063/K1071-K1073). Delta<.005 does NOT establish tied CE=lnV/ln2 or MSE=Var(y): initialization logit scale and target mean affect baseline loss. Do not turn weak architecture tendencies into a complete rank there. Nominal parity supplies no automatic adaptive-over-SGD tie-break(q_826eab),nor RMSprop-over-Adagrad law.
[K1015] MLP residual/depth at shared optimizer/lr/T: residual status is NOT a task-wide trump card. Older confounded corpus: deeper plain regression beats shallower residual24/39; classification deeper residual beats shallow plain33/47,shallow residual beats deep plain19/32. These counts do not isolate skips or justify 'never choose deep plain'. Terminal LN,activation,features and budget matter:K1061,K1065,K1033,K1074. q_6e56f3 at32epochs favors3-block plain over5-block residual; q_611798/q_bca005 reverse identical recipes across1/2-turn datasets. Deep residual appearance53% vs plain29% is not a matched comparison or universal residual+depth rank.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).
[K1017] Bigram post-LN TF,shared optimizer/lr/T,equal d_model: fewer layers favored atDelta.1-.5(old23/23);.02-.1 mixed8/15;below.02 deeper19/28 is WEAK. Changed FF/heads prevent a pure-depth or total-order inference. Old fewer-layer>=.5 wins8/11;23/23 comprises corpus6,lab17. Equal-depth largerFF:Delta<=.1 11/12(~1-2%CE),above3/13;not acrossdepth. Width:K1068;GRU:K1075;rate:K1071. q_162e81/q_a3b0c0 show low-progress depth misuse. Initialization and all shape dimensions matter;no universal depth-first/width-first sort.
[K1018] XOR CE,1024 rows,>=8 features,shared Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr/T,Delta>=.05: smooth is favored (older lab15/16, CE ratio.78; corpus6/6), but fewer LN is NOT validated. Fixed width24 depth2 plain GELU AdamW,T256,bs16: 2LN beat1LN at Delta .0256/.0512/.0768 (CE .67619 vs .68153 at .0768). Base-lab same optimizer type/lr, mixed architectures: moreLN36/51 high (37sets,ratio.891),14/32 low (26sets,1.001); older opposite LN counts use an unidentified filter.
